title.zh: 卷四百八十五 列傳第二百四十四 外國一 夏國上
title.en: Volume 485 Biographies 244: Foreign States 1 - State of Xia 1
title.raw: 卷四百八十五 列傳第二百四十四 外國一 夏國上 Volume 485 Biographies 244: Foreign States 1 - State of Xia 1

sentences.zh: 夏國上

translations.literal: State of Xia, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Western Xia (Part One)

sentences.zh: 昔唐承隋後，隋承周、齊，上溯元魏，故西北之疆有漢、晉正朔所不逮者，然亦不過使介之相通、貢聘之時至而已。

translations.literal: In former times Tang succeeded after Sui, Sui succeeded Zhou and Qi, tracing back to Northern Wei; thus in the northwest frontier were regions that the proper calendars of Han and Jin did not reach, yet this amounted only to having envoys pass messages and tribute missions arrive on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Tang succeeded the Sui, which in turn had succeeded the Zhou and Qi and looked back to the Northern Wei; the northwestern marches therefore included lands beyond the farthest reach of Han and Jin imperial authority, but relations never went beyond exchanging envoys and receiving tribute at appointed times.

sentences.zh: 唐德既衰，荒服不至，五季迭興，綱紀自紊，遠人慕義，無所適從。

translations.literal: When Tang virtue had declined, the distant domains no longer came; the Five Dynasties rose in succession, order itself became chaotic, and distant peoples who admired righteousness had nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: Once Tang moral authority waned, the outer realms ceased to present themselves; as the Five Dynasties rose one after another and imperial order dissolved, peoples of the far marches who wished to align with a righteous power found no clear lord to follow.

sentences.zh: 宋祖受命，諸國削平，海內清謐。

translations.literal: When the Song founder received the Mandate, the various states were reduced and pacified, and within the seas all was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: After the Song founder received Heaven's mandate, rival states were subdued and the realm within the Four Seas grew calm.

sentences.zh: 于是東若高麗、渤海，雖阻隔遼壤，而航海遠來，不憚跋涉。

translations.literal: Thereupon in the east, such as Koryŏ and Parhae, though separated by Liao territory, they came by sea from afar and did not shrink from the long journey.
translations.idiomatic: To the east, states such as Koryŏ and Parhae, though cut off by Liao lands, still sailed across the sea from afar without flinching at the hardship of the voyage.

sentences.zh: 西若天竺、于闐、回鶻、大食、高昌、龜茲、拂林等國，雖介遼、夏之間，筐篚亦至，屢勤館人。

translations.literal: In the west, such states as India, Khotan, the Uyghurs, Dashi, Gaochang, Kucha, and Fulin, though lying between Liao and Xia, still sent their baskets of tribute and repeatedly taxed the hosts of the reception offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the west, India, Khotan, the Uyghurs, the Arabs, Gaochang, Kucha, Byzantium, and the like—though their routes lay between Liao and Xia—still delivered tribute chests and kept the court's guest officers busy again and again.

sentences.zh: 党項、吐蕃唃廝囉董氈瞎征諸部，夏國兵力之所必爭者也，宋之威德亦暨其地，又間獲其助焉。

translations.literal: The Tangut, Tibetan Gusiluo, Dong Zhan, Xiazheng, and other tribes were territories that Xia military strength had to contest; Song majesty and virtue also reached these lands, and at times Song gained their aid as well.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut, the Tibetan Gusiluo, Dong Zhan, Xiazheng, and allied tribes were ground that Xia armies had to fight for, yet Song prestige and benevolence extended there too, and the court sometimes won their support.

sentences.zh: 交阯、占城、真臘、蒲耳、大理濱海諸蕃，自劉鋹、陳洪進來歸，接踵修貢。

translations.literal: Jiaozhi, Champa, Zhenla, Pu'er, Dali, and the coastal tribes—since Liu Chang and Chen Hongjin came to submit, they followed one after another in presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhi, Champa, Cambodia, Pu'er, Dali, and other maritime peoples along the southern coast, once Liu Chang and Chen Hongjin had submitted, sent tribute in steady succession.

sentences.zh: 宋之待遇亦得其道，厚其委積而不計其貢輸，假之榮名而不責以煩縟；

translations.literal: Song treatment of them also hit the right measure: enriching their stored gifts without reckoning their tribute deliveries, lending them honored titles without burdening them with troublesome formalities;
translations.idiomatic: The Song treated them with equal discernment: heaping gifts upon them without scrutinizing what they brought in tribute, granting them honorific titles without imposing vexatious protocol;

sentences.zh: 來則不拒，去則不追；

translations.literal: if they came, they were not refused; if they left, they were not pursued;
translations.idiomatic: those who came were not turned away, and those who left were not pursued;

sentences.zh: 邊圉相接，時有侵軼，命將致討，服則舍之，不黷以武。

translations.literal: where borders met, there were at times incursions; generals were ordered to chastise them, and once they submitted they were released, without abusing military force.
translations.idiomatic: where frontiers adjoined and raids occurred, the court sent generals to punish offenders and, once they submitted, let the matter rest without abusing arms.

sentences.zh: 先王柔遠之制豈復有加于是哉！

translations.literal: Could the former kings' system of gentle treatment of the distant go any further than this!
translations.idiomatic: Surely the ancient kings' policy of winning over distant peoples could scarcely have surpassed this!

sentences.zh: 南渡以後，朔漠不通，東南之陬以及西鄙，冠蓋猶有至者。

translations.literal: After the southward crossing, the northern deserts were no longer accessible; yet in the southeastern corners and the western marches, envoys in caps and coaches still came.
translations.idiomatic: After the court crossed south of the Yangzi, the northern steppe was cut off, yet in the southeast and along the western frontier diplomatic missions still arrived.

sentences.zh: 交人遠假爵命，訖宋亡而後絕焉。

translations.literal: The people of Jiaozhi long borrowed titles and commissions from afar, and only after Song perished did this cease.
translations.idiomatic: The Vietnamese long sought enfeoffment from the distant court, and only when the Song fell did that relationship end.

sentences.zh: 女直在宋初屢貢名馬，他日強大，修怨于遼，其索叛臣阿疏，責還所掠宋詔，猶知以通宋爲重；

translations.literal: The Jurchen in early Song repeatedly presented famous horses; when later they grew powerful and nursed grievances against Liao, in demanding the return of the rebel Ashu and censuring the seizure of Song imperial edicts, they still knew to value ties with Song;
translations.idiomatic: In the early Song the Jurchen often sent famous horses as tribute; when they later grew strong and turned against Liao, they still demanded the rebel Ashu back and protested the seizure of Song imperial edicts—showing they still prized relations with the Song;

sentences.zh: 及渝海上之盟，尋構大難，宋遂爲所絀辱，豈非自取之過乎！

translations.literal: When they violated the sea alliance and soon raised great calamity, Song was then subjected to their humiliation—was this not a fault of Song's own making!
translations.idiomatic: Once they broke the maritime alliance and soon brought catastrophe, the Song were left to their humiliation—was that not largely a calamity of their own making?

sentences.zh: 前宋舊史有《女直傳》，今既作《金史》，義當削之。

translations.literal: The former Song history had a 'Treatise on the Jurchen'; now that the 'History of Jin' has been compiled, by right it should be excised.
translations.idiomatic: The old Song History included a Jurchen treatise; now that a separate History of Jin exists, that chapter ought properly to be removed.

sentences.zh: 夏國雖亻面鄉不常，而視金有間，故仍舊史所錄存焉。

translations.literal: Although the State of Xia, though not constant in its orientation, yet in its view of Jin showed distance, therefore what the old history recorded is preserved here.
translations.idiomatic: Though Western Xia was fickle in its bearing toward the Song, it also kept a certain distance from Jin; for that reason the compilers retained the account from the older history.

sentences.zh: 李彝興，夏州人也，本姓拓跋氏。

translations.literal: Li Yixing was a man of Xia Prefecture; his original surname was Tuoba.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yixing was a native of Xia Prefecture and bore the surname Tuoba by birth.

sentences.zh: 唐貞觀初，有拓跋赤辭者歸唐，太宗賜姓李，置靜邊等州以處之。

translations.literal: In early Zhenguan of Tang there was Tuoba Chici who submitted to Tang; Taizong bestowed the surname Li and established Jingbian and other prefectures to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign, Tuoba Chici came over to the Tang, and Emperor Taizong granted the Li surname and established Jingbian and other prefectures to receive his people.

sentences.zh: 其後析居夏州者號平夏部。

translations.literal: Later those who split off and dwelt at Xia Prefecture were called the Pingxia tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Those who later settled separately at Xia Prefecture came to be known as the Pingxia branch.

sentences.zh: 唐末，拓跋思恭鎮夏州，統銀、夏、綏、宥、靜五州地，討黃巢有功，復賜李姓。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang, Tuoba Sigong governed Xia Prefecture, ruling the five prefectures of Yin, Xia, Sui, You, and Jing; he had merit in campaigning against Huang Chao and was again granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tang, Tuoba Sigong held Xia Prefecture and controlled Yin, Xia, Sui, You, and Jing; for his service against Huang Chao he was again granted the Li surname.

sentences.zh: 思恭卒，弟思諫代爲定難軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Sigong died, his younger brother Sijian succeeded him as military commissioner of Dingnan.
translations.idiomatic: After Sigong's death his younger brother Sijian became military commissioner of the Dingnan army.

sentences.zh: 思諫卒，思恭孫彝昌嗣。

translations.literal: When Sijian died, Sigong's grandson Yichang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Sijian died, Sigong's grandson Yichang took his place.

sentences.zh: 梁開平中，彝昌遇害，將士立其族子蕃部指揮仁福。

translations.literal: In Kaiping of Liang, Yichang met with violence; the officers and soldiers installed his clansman, the tribal commander Renfu, in his place.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liang Kaiping era Yichang was killed, and the troops raised his kinsman Renfu, a tribal commander, to lead them.

sentences.zh: 仁福卒，子彝超嗣。

translations.literal: When Renfu died, his son Yichao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Renfu was succeeded by his son Yichao.

sentences.zh: 事具《五代史》。

translations.literal: The full account is in the History of the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The details are recorded in the History of the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加太尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was promoted to Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Song he was made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 北漢劉鈞結代北諸部來寇麟州，彝興遣部將李彝玉會諸鎮兵禦之，鈞衆遂引去。

translations.literal: Liu Jun of Northern Han joined the tribes north of Dai to raid Lin Prefecture; Yixing sent his subordinate general Li Yiyu to join the garrison forces of the various circuits in defense, and Jun's host then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jun of Northern Han allied with the northern tribes to attack Lin Prefecture, Yixing sent Li Yiyu with allied frontier troops to resist, and Jun's forces withdrew.

sentences.zh: 建隆初，獻馬三百匹，太祖大喜，親視攻玉爲帶，且召使問曰：「汝帥腹圍幾何？

translations.literal: In early Jianlong he presented three hundred horses; Taizu was greatly pleased, personally watched the jade-carving of a belt, and also summoned the envoy, asking: 'How large is your commander's waist?'
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianlong era he sent three hundred horses as tribute. The Taizu emperor was delighted, personally oversaw the carving of a jade belt, and summoned the envoy to ask, 'How large around is your commander's waist?'

sentences.zh: 」使言：「彝興腰復甚大。

translations.literal: ' The envoy said: 'Yixing's waist and belly are very large.'
translations.idiomatic: The envoy replied, 'Yixing has a very large waist.'

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「汝帥真福人也。

translations.literal: ' Taizu said: 'Your commander is truly a man of good fortune.'
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu emperor said, 'Your commander is truly a blessed man.'

sentences.zh: 」遂遣使以帶賜之。

translations.literal: ' He then sent an envoy to bestow the belt upon him.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent an envoy to present the belt as a gift.

sentences.zh: 乾德五年，卒，太祖廢朝三日，贈太師，追封夏王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiande he died; Taizu suspended court for three days, posthumously appointed him Grand Preceptor, and enfeoffed him posthumously as King of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Qiande. The Taizu emperor mourned him with three days without court, posthumously made him Grand Preceptor, and enfeoffed him as King of Xia.

sentences.zh: 子克睿立。

translations.literal: His son Kerui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kerui succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 克睿初名光睿，避太宗諱改「光」爲「克」。

translations.literal: Kerui was originally named Guangrui; to avoid the taboo of Taizong he changed 'Guang' to 'Ke.'
translations.idiomatic: Kerui had originally been named Guangrui; to avoid the taboo on the character guang used in the Taizong emperor's name, he changed it to ke.

sentences.zh: 彝興之卒，自權知州事，授檢校太保、定難軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Yixing died, he himself assumed provisional charge of prefectural affairs and was appointed Acting Grand Guardian and military commissioner of Dingnan.
translations.idiomatic: On Yixing's death he took provisional control of the prefecture and was appointed Acting Grand Guardian and military commissioner of the Dingnan army.

sentences.zh: 開寶九年，率兵破北漢吳堡砦，斬首七百級，獲牛羊千計，俘砦主侯遇以獻，累加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaibao he led troops and captured the Northern Han fort of Wubao, beheading seven hundred, taking cattle and sheep by the thousands, and capturing the fort commander Hou Yu to present; he was repeatedly promoted to Acting Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kaibao he stormed the Northern Han fort at Wubao, took seven hundred heads, seized thousands of cattle and sheep, and sent the fort commander Hou Yu as a captive; he was eventually promoted to Acting Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，卒，太宗廢朝二日，贈侍中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he died; Taizong suspended court for two days and posthumously appointed him Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Taiping Xingguo. The Taizong emperor observed two days of mourning and posthumously made him Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 子繼筠立。

translations.literal: His son Jiyun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiyun succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 繼筠，初爲衙內都指揮使、檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: Jiyun was at first commander of the inner guard and Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyun had first served as commander of the inner guard and Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 克睿卒，自權知州事，授檢校司徒、定難軍節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: When Kerui died, he himself assumed provisional charge of prefectural affairs and was appointed Acting Minister of Education and surveillance commissioner and acting military commissioner of Dingnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Kerui died he took provisional control of the prefecture and was appointed Acting Minister of Education, surveillance commissioner, and acting military commissioner of Dingnan.

sentences.zh: 太宗征北漢，繼筠遣銀州刺史李光遠、綏州刺史李光憲率蕃、漢兵列陣渡河，略太原境以張軍勢。

translations.literal: When Taizong campaigned against Northern Han, Jiyun sent the prefect of Yin Li Guangyuan and the prefect of Sui Li Guangxian to lead tribal and Han troops in battle array across the river, raiding the Taiyuan region to display military strength.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taizong emperor's campaign against Northern Han, Jiyun sent the Yin prefect Li Guangyuan and the Sui prefect Li Guangxian with mixed tribal and Han forces across the river to harry the Taiyuan frontier and magnify the Song army's presence.

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年，卒，弟繼捧立。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo he died; his younger brother Jipeng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo and was succeeded by his younger brother Jipeng.

sentences.zh: 繼捧立，以太平興國七年率族人入朝。

translations.literal: When Jipeng succeeded, in the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo he led his clansmen to court.
translations.idiomatic: After Jipeng took power, in the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo he led his kinsmen to the capital.

sentences.zh: 自上世以來，未嘗親覲者，繼捧至，太宗甚嘉之，賜白金千兩、帛千匹、錢百萬。

translations.literal: From the upper generations none had ever come in person to audience; when Jipeng arrived, Taizong greatly commended him and bestowed a thousand taels of white gold, a thousand bolts of silk, and a million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: No one in his line had ever presented himself at court in person before; when Jipeng came, the Taizong emperor praised him warmly and gave him a thousand taels of silver, a thousand bolts of silk, and a million in cash.

sentences.zh: 祖母獨孤氏亦獻玉盤一、金盤三，皆厚賚之。

translations.literal: His grandmother Lady Dugu also presented one jade dish and three gold dishes, and all were richly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother, Lady Dugu of the Dugu clan, also presented one jade platter and three gold platters, and the court rewarded them generously.

sentences.zh: 繼捧陳其諸父、昆弟多相怨，願留京師。

translations.literal: Jipeng stated that his uncles and brothers were much at odds with one another and that he wished to remain in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jipeng explained that his uncles and brothers were bitterly divided and asked to remain at the capital.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使夏州護緦麻已上親赴闕，授繼捧彰德軍節度使，並官其昆弟夏州蕃落指揮使克信等十二人有差，遂曲赦銀、夏管內。

translations.literal: An envoy was then sent to Xia Prefecture to escort relatives in mourning dress and above to court; Jipeng was appointed military commissioner of Zhangde, and his brothers including the Xia tribal commander Kexin and eleven others were given offices of varying rank; a special amnesty was then granted within Yin and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent envoys to Xia to bring kinsmen in the prescribed mourning grades to the capital, made Jipeng military commissioner of Zhangde, and appointed twelve of his brothers, including the tribal commander Kexin, to various posts; a general amnesty was then proclaimed for the Yin and Xia region.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗宴群臣苑中，謂繼捧曰：「汝在夏州用何道以制諸部？

translations.literal: Taizong once feasted the ministers in the imperial park and said to Jipeng: 'When you were at Xia Prefecture, by what method did you control the various tribes?'
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong emperor once entertained his ministers in the imperial park and asked Jipeng, 'When you were at Xia Prefecture, how did you keep the tribes in hand?'

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「羌人鷙悍，但羈糜而已，非能制也。

translations.literal: ' He replied: 'The Qiang are fierce and stubborn; one can only tether and feed them—that is all—not truly control them.'
translations.idiomatic: He answered, 'The Qiang are fierce and unruly; one can only keep them on a loose tether with gifts—one cannot truly control them.'

sentences.zh: 」弟權知夏州克文來朝，以唐僖宗所賜其祖思恭鐵券及朱書御劄來上，改博州防禦使。

translations.literal: ' His younger brother, provisional prefect of Xia Kewen, came to court and presented the iron certificate and vermilion imperial letter that Emperor Xizong of Tang had bestowed on their grandfather Sigong; he was transferred to Defender of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Kewen, who was acting prefect of Xia, came to court and presented the iron certificate and vermilion imperial rescript that Tang Emperor Xizong had granted their grandfather Sigong; he was reassigned as Defender of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 初，繼捧之入也，弟繼遷出奔，及是，數來爲邊患。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jipeng entered court, his younger brother Jiqian had fled; by this time he repeatedly came as a border menace.
translations.idiomatic: When Jipeng first came to court, his younger brother Jiqian had fled into the wilds; by now Jiqian was raiding the frontier again and again.

sentences.zh: 有言繼遷悉知朝廷事，蓋繼捧泄之。

translations.literal: Some said Jiqian knew all the court's affairs, and that Jipeng had leaked them.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread that Jiqian knew everything happening at court—supposedly because Jipeng had betrayed it.

sentences.zh: 乃出爲崇信軍節度使，克憲爲道州防禦使，克文遣歸博州，並選常參官爲通判，以專郡政。

translations.literal: He was then sent out as military commissioner of Chongxin, Kexian became Defender of Daozhou, Kewen was sent back to Bozhou, and regular-attendance officials were chosen as deputy prefects to monopolize prefectural administration.
translations.idiomatic: Jipeng was transferred to military commissioner of Chongxin, Kexian was made Defender of Daozhou, Kewen was sent back to Bozhou, and regular court officials were appointed as deputy prefects to keep tight control of local government.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，改感德軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was transferred to military commissioner of Gande.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Duangong era he was reassigned as military commissioner of Gande.

sentences.zh: 屢發兵討繼遷不克，用宰相趙普計，欲委繼捧以邊事，令圖之。

translations.literal: Troops were repeatedly sent to campaign against Jiqian without success; adopting the plan of the chief minister Zhao Pu, they wished to entrust Jipeng with frontier affairs and have him devise a strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated campaigns against Jiqian failed. Following Chief Minister Zhao Pu's advice, the court decided to put Jipeng back in charge of the frontier and have him deal with Jiqian.

sentences.zh: 因召赴闕，賜姓趙氏，更名保忠，太宗親書五色金花箋以賜之，授夏州刺史，充定難軍節度使、夏銀綏宥靜等州觀察處置押蕃落等使。

translations.literal: He was therefore summoned to court, granted the surname Zhao, and renamed Baozhong; Taizong personally wrote a five-colored gold-flowered letter to bestow on him, appointed him prefect of Xia, and made him military commissioner of Dingnan, surveillance and disposal commissioner for Xia, Yin, Sui, You, Jing, and other prefectures, and commissioner for overseeing the tribal peoples.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court, granted the imperial Zhao surname, and renamed Baozhong. The Taizong emperor personally wrote him a letter on five-colored gold-flowered paper and appointed him prefect of Xia, military commissioner of Dingnan, and commissioner overseeing Xia, Yin, Sui, You, Jing, and the tribal peoples of the region.

sentences.zh: 賜金器千兩、銀器萬兩，並賜五州錢帛、芻粟、田園。

translations.literal: He was bestowed a thousand taels of gold vessels and ten thousand taels of silver vessels, and also given money, silk, fodder, grain, and estates in the five prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He received a thousand taels' worth of gold vessels and ten thousand taels' worth of silver, along with cash, silk, fodder, grain, and estates across the five prefectures.

sentences.zh: 保忠辭日，宴于長春殿，賜襲衣、玉帶、銀鞍馬、錦彩三千匹、銀器三千兩，又賜錦袍、銀帶五百，副馬百匹。

translations.literal: On the day Baozhong took leave, he was feasted in the Changchun Hall and bestowed court robes, a jade belt, a silver saddle and horse, three thousand bolts of brocade, three thousand taels of silver vessels, and also five hundred brocade robes and silver belts and a hundred spare horses.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he departed, the court feasted him in the Changchun Hall and gave him court dress, a jade belt, a silver-mounted horse, three thousand bolts of brocade, three thousand taels of silverware, five hundred brocade robes with silver belts, and a hundred spare mounts.

sentences.zh: 至鎮數月，上言繼遷悔過歸款，乃授繼遷官，然實無降心也。

translations.literal: Several months after reaching his post, he memorialized that Jiqian repented his faults and submitted; Jiqian was then given an office, yet in truth he had no heart to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: A few months after he took up his post, he reported that Jiqian wished to repent and submit; the court gave Jiqian an office, but he had no real intention of yielding.

sentences.zh: 二年，加保忠特進、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted for Baozhong to Special Advancement and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Baozhong was made Special Advancement and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，與繼遷戰于安慶澤，繼遷中流矢遁去。

translations.literal: In early Chunhua he fought Jiqian at Anqing Marsh; Jiqian was struck by an arrow and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chunhua era he fought Jiqian at Anqing Marsh; Jiqian took an arrow wound and fled.

sentences.zh: 保忠乞師禦繼遷，遣商州團練使翟守素率兵援之。

translations.literal: Baozhong requested troops to resist Jiqian; the training commissioner of Shangzhou Zhai Shousu was sent to lead troops to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhong asked for reinforcements against Jiqian, and Zhai Shousu, training commissioner of Shangzhou, was sent with an army to support him.

sentences.zh: 賜保忠茶百斤、上醞十石。

translations.literal: Baozhong was bestowed a hundred jin of tea and ten shi of fine wine.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave Baozhong a hundred jin of tea and ten shi of fine wine.

sentences.zh: 乃獻白鶻，名海東青，以久罷畋獵，詔慰還之。

translations.literal: He then presented a white gyrfalcon named 'Sea East Green'; because hunting had long been suspended, an edict comforted him and returned it.
translations.idiomatic: He then presented a white gyrfalcon called Sea East Green; because the court had long suspended falconry, an edict thanked him and sent the bird back.

sentences.zh: 五年，繼遷攻靈州，遣侍衛馬軍都指揮使李繼隆討之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Jiqian attacked Ling Prefecture; the commander of the palace horse guard Li Jilong was sent to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Jiqian attacked Ling Prefecture, and Li Jilong, commander of the palace horse guard, was dispatched against him.

sentences.zh: 保忠先挈其母與妻子壁野外，乃上言與繼遷解怨，獻馬五十匹，乞罷兵。

translations.literal: Baozhong first took his mother and wife and children to fortify themselves in the open country, then memorialized that he and Jiqian had settled their grievances, presented fifty horses, and begged to halt the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhong first moved his mother, wife, and children to a fortified camp in the open, then reported that he and Jiqian had made peace, sent fifty horses as tribute, and asked that the campaign be stopped.

sentences.zh: 帝覽奏，立遣中使督繼隆進軍。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and immediately sent a palace envoy to urge Jilong to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the report and at once sent a palace envoy to order Jilong forward.

sentences.zh: 及兵壓境，保忠反爲繼遷所圖，欲並其衆，縛牙校趙光祚，襲其營帳。

translations.literal: When the army pressed the border, Baozhong in turn was plotted against by Jiqian, who wished to absorb his forces; he bound the adjutant Zhao Guangzuo and raided his camp.
translations.idiomatic: As the army closed in, Jiqian turned on Baozhong, hoping to absorb his troops; he bound Baozhong's adjutant Zhao Guangzuo and attacked his camp.

sentences.zh: 保忠方寢，聞難作，單騎走還城，爲大校趙光嗣閉于別室，旦開門迎繼隆，乃執保忠送闕下，待罪崇政殿庭。

translations.literal: Baozhong was just asleep; hearing trouble arise, he fled alone on horseback back to the city, was shut in a side room by the senior officer Zhao Guangsi, and at dawn the gates were opened to welcome Jilong; Baozhong was then seized and sent to court, awaiting judgment in the courtyard of the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhong was asleep when the attack began; he rode alone back to the city, where the senior officer Zhao Guangsi locked him in a side room. At dawn the gates were opened to admit Jilong, and Baozhong was seized and sent to court to await judgment in the Chongzheng Hall courtyard.

sentences.zh: 帝詰責數四，釋之，賜冠帶、器幣，並賜其母金銀器以撫之。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him several times, then released him, bestowing cap and belt and vessels and silks, and also bestowing gold and silver vessels on his mother to comfort her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him repeatedly, then pardoned him, gave him cap, belt, and gifts, and sent gold and silver vessels to his mother by way of consolation.

sentences.zh: 尋責授右千牛衛上將軍，封宥罪侯，賜第京師。

translations.literal: Soon he was demoted and appointed Senior General of the Right Palace Guard, enfeoffed as Marquis of Pardoned Fault, and granted a mansion in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon demoted to Senior General of the Right Palace Guard, enfeoffed as Marquis of Pardoned Fault, and given a house in the capital.

sentences.zh: 保忠狀貌雄毅，居環列，奉朝請，常怏怏不自得。

translations.literal: Baozhong's bearing was bold and stern; he dwelt among the outer ranks as a court attendant and was often discontent and ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhong was a man of imposing presence; he lived among the outer courtiers as a regular attendant and was often sullen and dissatisfied.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，丁內艱，以本官起復，遷右金吾衛上將軍，判岳州，移復州。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era he entered mourning for his mother, resumed office in his former post, was transferred to Senior General of the Right Golden Crow Guard, assigned to Yue Prefecture, and then moved to Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping era he mourned his mother, then resumed duty in his former rank, was made Senior General of the Right Golden Crow Guard, served as prefect of Yue, and was later transferred to Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 景德元年病劇，上言有子永哥不肖，乞配春州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde his illness grew severe; he memorialized that his son Yongge was unworthy and begged that he be banished to Chun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingde his illness worsened; he reported that his son Yongge was worthless and asked that he be exiled to Chun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帝以其病語，乃授永州別駕，詔監軍察之。

translations.literal: The emperor, taking this as the speech of his illness, appointed Yongge Vice-Prefect of Yongzhou and ordered the military supervisor to watch him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, attributing the request to his illness, made Yongge Vice-Prefect of Yongzhou and ordered the military inspector to keep watch on him.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈威塞軍節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he died and was posthumously appointed military commissioner of Weisai.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died and was posthumously made military commissioner of Weisai.

sentences.zh: 克文亦死，贈岳州防禦使。

translations.literal: Kewen also died and was posthumously appointed Defender of Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Kewen also died and was posthumously made Defender of Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天禧四年，錄其孫從吉爲三班奉職。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianxi his grandson Congji was enrolled as a third-rank attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianxi his grandson Congji was enrolled in the third-rank attendant service.

sentences.zh: 繼遷，繼捧族弟也。

translations.literal: Jiqian was a clansman and younger cousin of Jipeng.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqian was Jipeng's clansman and younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 高祖思忠，嘗從兄思恭討黃巢，拒賊于渭橋，表有鐵鶴，射之沒羽，賊駭之，遂先士卒，戰沒，僖宗贈宥州刺史，祠于渭陽。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Sizhong once followed his elder cousin Sigong in campaigning against Huang Chao; he blocked the rebels at Weiqiao, where on the watchtower was an iron crane; he shot it and the arrow sank to the feathers; the rebels were terrified; he then led the vanguard and died in battle; Emperor Xizong posthumously appointed him prefect of You and enshrined him north of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Sizhong had followed his cousin Sigong against Huang Chao and held the rebels at Weiqiao. When he shot an iron crane on the watchtower so that the arrow sank to its feathers, the rebels were terrified. He then led the charge and fell in battle. Emperor Xizong posthumously made him prefect of You and had him enshrined north of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 曾祖仁顏，仕唐，銀州防禦使。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Renyan served Tang as Defender of Yin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Renyan had served the Tang as Defender of Yin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖彝景嗣于晉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yijing succeeded under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yijing had succeeded under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 父光儼嗣于周。

translations.literal: His father Guangyan succeeded under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guangyan had succeeded under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年，繼遷生于銀州無定河，生而有齒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianlong Jiqian was born on the Wuding River in Yin Prefecture; he was born with teeth.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianlong he was born on the Wuding River in Yin Prefecture, already with teeth.

sentences.zh: 開寶七年，授定難軍管內都知蕃落使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kaibao he was appointed commissioner in charge of all tribal peoples within the Dingnan army circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Kaibao he was made commissioner overseeing all tribal peoples within the Dingnan circuit.

sentences.zh: 繼捧之歸宋，時年二十，留居銀州，及使至，召緦麻親赴闕，乃詐言乳母死，出葬于郊，遂與其黨數十人奔入地斤澤，澤距夏州東北三百里。

translations.literal: When Jipeng submitted to Song, Jiqian was twenty and remained at Yin Prefecture; when the envoy arrived summoning relatives in mourning dress to court, he falsely claimed his wet-nurse had died, went out to bury her in the suburbs, and then with several dozen followers fled into the Dijin Marsh, three hundred li northeast of Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Jipeng submitted to the Song, Jiqian was twenty and stayed at Yin Prefecture. When envoys came to summon kinsmen in mourning to court, he pretended his wet-nurse had died, went out for a suburban burial, and fled with several dozen followers into the Dijin Marsh, three hundred li northeast of Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太平興國八年，知夏州尹憲與都巡檢曹光實偵知，夜襲破之，斬首五百級，焚四百餘帳。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo the prefect of Xia Yin Xian and the chief inspector Cao Guangshi learned by reconnaissance and raided him by night, beheading five hundred and burning more than four hundred tents.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo the Xia prefect Yin Xian and chief inspector Cao Guangshi scouted his camp and struck by night, taking five hundred heads and burning more than four hundred tents.

sentences.zh: 繼遷與其弟遁免，獲其母與妻。

translations.literal: Jiqian and his younger brother escaped; his mother and wife were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqian and his brother escaped, but his mother and wife were taken.

sentences.zh: 繼遷復連娶豪族，轉遷無常，漸以強大，而西人以李氏世著恩德，往往多歸之。

translations.literal: Jiqian again married into powerful clans in succession, moved about without fixed abode, and gradually grew strong; the western peoples, because the Li clan had long shown grace and virtue, often came over to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqian married into powerful families one after another, shifted camp constantly, and slowly grew strong. Because the Li clan had long enjoyed prestige in the west, many tribesmen rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 繼遷因語其豪右曰：「李氏世有西土，今一旦絕之，爾等不忘李氏，能從我興復乎？

translations.literal: Jiqian therefore said to the tribal leaders: 'The Li clan for generations held the western lands; now it has been cut off at once. You who have not forgotten the Li—can you follow me to restore it?'
translations.idiomatic: Jiqian told the tribal leaders, 'The Li have held the western lands for generations, and now that hold is gone in a day. You who have not forgotten the Li—will you follow me to restore it?'

sentences.zh: 」衆曰：「諾。

translations.literal: ' The crowd said: 'We agree.'
translations.idiomatic: They answered, 'We will.'

sentences.zh: 」遂與弟繼沖、破醜重遇貴、張浦、李大信等起夏州，乃詐降，誘殺曹光實于葭蘆川，遂襲銀州據之，時雍熙二年二月也。

translations.literal: ' He then rose at Xia Prefecture with his younger brother Jichong, Pochou, Chongyugui, Zhang Pu, Li Daxin, and others; he feigned surrender and lured Cao Guangshi to his death at Jialu River, then raided and seized Yin Prefecture—it was the second month of the second year of Yongxi.
translations.idiomatic: He then rose at Xia with his brother Jichong, Pochou, Chongyugui, Zhang Pu, Li Daxin, and others. Feigning submission, he lured Cao Guangshi to his death on the Jialu River, seized Yin Prefecture, and held it—in the second month of the second year of Yongxi.

sentences.zh: 三月，破會州，焚毀城郭而去。

translations.literal: In the third month he captured Hui Prefecture, burned the walls and towers, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he stormed Hui Prefecture, burned the city, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三年，遼以義成公主嫁繼遷，冊爲夏國王。

translations.literal: In the third year Liao married the Princess Yicheng to Jiqian and enfeoffed him as King of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Liao married Princess Yicheng to him and enfeoffed him as King of Xia.

sentences.zh: 四年，知夏州安守忠以三萬衆戰于王亭鎮，敗績，繼遷追至城門而返。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the prefect of Xia An Shouzhong fought at Wangting Town with thirty thousand men and was defeated; Jiqian pursued to the city gate and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Xia prefect An Shouzhong fought him at Wangting with thirty thousand men and was defeated; Jiqian pursued to the city gate and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 端拱元年，繼捧之節制夏台，言能歸款，即授洛苑使、銀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duangong, under Jipeng's command over Xia, he said he could submit; he was at once appointed Luoyuan Commissioner and prefect of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Duangong, while Jipeng held authority over Xia, Jiqian said he would submit and was made Luoyuan Commissioner and prefect of Yin.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，復與繼捧戰于安慶澤，不利。

translations.literal: In early Chunhua he again fought Jipeng at Anqing Marsh and fared ill.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chunhua era he fought Jipeng again at Anqing Marsh and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 轉攻夏州，繼捧乞師，及翟守素來，又奉表歸款，授銀州觀察，賜名保吉，子德明管內蕃落使、行軍司馬。

translations.literal: He then turned to attack Xia Prefecture; Jipeng begged for troops, and when Zhai Shousu came he again submitted a memorial of surrender, was appointed surveillance commissioner of Yin, granted the name Baoji, and his son Deming was made commissioner of tribal peoples within the circuit and army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He then attacked Xia Prefecture. Jipeng called for reinforcements, and when Zhai Shousu arrived Jiqian submitted again, was made surveillance commissioner of Yin, given the name Baoji, and his son Deming was appointed commissioner of tribal peoples and army marshal.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，轉運副使鄭文寶議禁鹽池，用困繼遷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua, Transportation Vice Commissioner Zheng Wenbao proposed banning the salt ponds to use [the measure] to distress Jiqian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chunhua, Transportation Vice Commissioner Zheng Wenbao proposed closing the salt ponds to choke off Jiqian.

sentences.zh: 數月，邊人四十二族萬餘騎寇環州，屠小康堡，太宗乃遣錢若水弛其禁，因撫慰之。

translations.literal: After several months, more than ten thousand horsemen of forty-two frontier tribes raided Huan Prefecture and slaughtered Xiaokang Fort; Taizong then sent Qian Ruoshui to relax the ban and thereby comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Within months, tribesmen of forty-two frontier groups—more than ten thousand cavalry strong—raided Huan Prefecture and massacred Xiaokang Fort. Emperor Taizong sent Qian Ruoshui to lift the ban and soothe them.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，繼遷徙綏州民于平夏，部將高文岯等因衆不樂反，攻敗之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, Jiqian moved the people of Sui Prefecture to Pingxia; his subordinate general Gao Wenqi and others, because the people were discontented, rebelled and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year Jiqian relocated the people of Sui Prefecture to Pingxia. Subordinate general Gao Wenqi and others rebelled when the populace grew restive and routed him.

sentences.zh: 繼遷復圍堡砦，掠居民，焚積聚，遂攻靈州，詔遣李繼隆等進討。

translations.literal: Jiqian again besieged forts and stockades, plundered inhabitants, burned stored goods, then attacked Ling Prefecture; an edict dispatched Li Jilong and others to advance and punish.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqian again besieged forts and outposts, looted the populace, and burned stores, then attacked Ling Prefecture. The court ordered Li Jilong and others to march against him.

sentences.zh: 繼遷夜襲保忠，走之，獲其輜重以歸。

translations.literal: Jiqian raided Baozhong by night, put him to flight, and returned with his baggage train captured.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqian struck Baozhong in a night attack, drove him off, and returned with his supply train as booty.

sentences.zh: 七月，乃獻馬以謝。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he then presented horses to express thanks.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he sent horses as a gesture of conciliation.

sentences.zh: 又遣弟廷信獻馬、橐駝，太宗撫賚甚厚，遣內侍張崇貴詔諭，賜茶藥、器幣、衣物。

translations.literal: He again sent his younger brother Tingxin to present horses and camels; Taizong treated them with great gifts and comfort, dispatched palace attendant Zhang Chonggui with an edict to instruct him, and bestowed tea, medicines, vessels, silks, and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his brother Tingxin with horses and camels. Taizong rewarded them lavishly, sent palace attendant Zhang Chonggui with an edict of instruction, and granted tea, medicines, vessels, silks, and clothing.

sentences.zh: 至道初，遣左都押衙張浦以橐駝、良馬來獻。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao he dispatched Left Chief Military Instructor Zhang Pu to come presenting camels and fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhidao era he sent Left Chief Military Instructor Zhang Pu with camels and fine horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 太宗令衛士翹關、超乘、引強、奪槊于後園，俾浦等觀，且令兵士皆拓兩石弓。

translations.literal: Taizong had the guards perform lifting gates, vaulting onto horses, drawing strong bows, and seizing spears in the rear garden for Pu and the others to observe, and moreover had the soldiers all draw two-stone bows.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had his guards perform gate-lifting, vaulting, strong-bow drawing, and spear contests in the rear garden for Pu and his party to watch, and ordered the soldiers to draw two-stone bows.

sentences.zh: 帝笑問浦曰：「羌人敢敵否？

translations.literal: The emperor said smiling to Pu: "Do the Qiang dare to fight?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and asked Pu, "Would the Qiang dare stand against such men?"

sentences.zh: 」浦曰：「羌部弓弱矢短，但見此長大人則已遁矣，況敢敵乎！

translations.literal: Pu said: "Qiang tribes' bows are weak and arrows short; upon seeing such tall men they would already flee—how much less dare to fight!"
translations.idiomatic: Pu answered, "The Qiang use weak bows and short arrows. At the sight of such tall warriors they would already flee—let alone fight them!"

sentences.zh: 」繼遷乞禁邊盜掠，詔令謹守疆場，還所盜物。

translations.literal: Jiqian begged that frontier pillaging be forbidden; an edict ordered strict guarding of the border and return of stolen goods.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqian asked that frontier raids be suppressed. An edict ordered strict border discipline and the return of all stolen property.

sentences.zh: 遣閣門副使馮訥、中使賈繼隆持詔拜繼遷鄜州節度使，不受。

translations.literal: He dispatched Gate Deputy Commissioner Feng Ne and imperial envoy Jia Jilong bearing an edict to invest Jiqian as military commissioner of Bian Prefecture; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Gate Deputy Commissioner Feng Ne and imperial envoy Jia Jilong with an edict appointing Jiqian military commissioner of Bian, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 乃以浦爲鄭州團練，留京師。

translations.literal: Pu was then made regimental trainer of Zheng Prefecture and kept in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was made regimental trainer of Zheng Prefecture and kept at court.

sentences.zh: 繼遷表鄭文寶誘其部長嵬囉、嵬悉，遂貶文寶藍山令。

translations.literal: Jiqian memorialized that Zheng Wenbao had seduced his tribal chiefs Weiluo and Weixi; Wenbao was then demoted to magistrate of Lanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqian reported that Zheng Wenbao had suborned his chiefs Weiluo and Weixi, and Wenbao was demoted to magistrate of Lanshan.

sentences.zh: 繼遷以千騎攻清遠軍，守臣張延擊退之。

translations.literal: Jiqian with a thousand horsemen attacked Qingyuan Army; the defending official Zhang Yan struck and repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqian attacked Qingyuan Army with a thousand cavalry; defender Zhang Yan drove him back.

sentences.zh: 二年春，命洛苑使白守榮等護送芻粟四十萬于靈州，且令車重先後作三隊，丁夫持弓矢自衛，士卒布方陣以護之，遇敵則戰，可以無失。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year he ordered Luoyuan Commissioner Bai Shourong and others to escort four hundred thousand [units] of fodder and grain to Ling Prefecture, and moreover ordered the wagons and heavy baggage to form three squads in succession, laborers to carry bows and arrows for self-defense, and soldiers to deploy in square formations to protect them; encountering the enemy they would fight, and thus could be without loss.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year the court ordered Luoyuan Commissioner Bai Shourong and others to escort four hundred thousand bundles of fodder and grain to Ling Prefecture. The wagons were to travel in three successive columns, laborers armed with bows for self-defense, and soldiers in square formations for protection—fighting if attacked, so that nothing would be lost.

sentences.zh: 復令會州觀察使田紹斌率兵應援。

translations.literal: He further ordered Hui Prefecture Surveillance Commissioner Tian Shaobin to lead troops in reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Shaobin, surveillance commissioner of Hui Prefecture, was also ordered to bring troops in support.

sentences.zh: 而守榮乃並爲一運，繼遷邀擊于浦洛河，紹斌不救，衆潰，運饋盡爲繼遷所得。

translations.literal: But Shourong combined them into one convoy; Jiqian intercepted at the Pulu River, Shaobin did not rescue, the force collapsed, and the entire supply train fell to Jiqian.
translations.idiomatic: Shourong, however, combined everything into a single convoy. Jiqian ambushed it on the Pulu River; Shaobin failed to intervene, the force scattered, and Jiqian captured the entire supply train.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞之怒。

translations.literal: Taizong, hearing this, grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong heard of it he was furious.

sentences.zh: 四月，復命李繼隆爲環、慶等州都部署。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he again appointed Li Jilong overall commander of Huan, Qing, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Li Jilong was again made overall commander of Huan, Qing, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 會四方館使曹璨自河西至，言繼遷衆萬余圍靈武，城中上表告急，爲繼遷所得，遂頓兵不去。

translations.literal: At this time Four Directions Commissioner Cao Shen arrived from Hexi and reported that Jiqian with more than ten thousand men was besieging Lingwu; the city's urgent memorial had been captured by Jiqian, who therefore halted his troops and did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Four Directions Commissioner Cao Shen arrived from Hexi reporting that Jiqian had more than ten thousand men besieging Lingwu. The city's urgent petition had been intercepted by Jiqian, who therefore kept his army in place.

sentences.zh: 時朝議或云率輕騎三道搗平夏；

translations.literal: At the time court deliberation had some who said to lead light cavalry in three columns to strike Pingxia;
translations.idiomatic: Court debate split: some urged three columns of light cavalry to strike Pingxia directly;

sentences.zh: 或云暑涉旱海無水泉，糧運艱辛，不如靜以待之，帝不聽。

translations.literal: others who said that in summer one crosses the dry sea without springs, supply transport is arduous, and it is better to wait quietly—the emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: others argued that summer marches across the dry sea meant no water, supply lines would be brutal, and the court should wait—the emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 九月，親部分諸將，繼隆出環州，丁罕出慶州，範廷召出延州，王超出夏州，張守恩出鄜州，五路進討，直抵平夏。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he personally divided the generals: Jilong out from Huan, Ding Han from Qing, Fan Tingzhao from Yan, Wang Chao from Xia, Zhang Shou'en from Bian—five routes advancing to punish, straight to Pingxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he personally deployed his generals: Jilong from Huan, Ding Han from Qing, Fan Tingzhao from Yan, Wang Chao from Xia, and Zhang Shou'en from Bian—five armies marching on Pingxia.

sentences.zh: 繼隆以環州路迂，乃自青岡峽繞靈武徑趨平夏，兵行數日，與丁罕合，又行十餘日無所見，乃引還。

translations.literal: Jilong, because the Huan route was circuitous, from Qinggang Gorge circled Lingwu and hastened directly to Pingxia; the army marched several days, joined Ding Han, marched more than ten days without finding anything, and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the Huan route too long, Jilong cut through Qinggang Gorge via Lingwu straight toward Pingxia. After several days he joined Ding Han; after ten more days with no enemy in sight, he turned back.

sentences.zh: 張守恩遇之，不戰而遁。

translations.literal: Zhang Shou'en encountered him and fled without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shou'en met him and fled without a fight.

sentences.zh: 王超、範廷召遇之于烏白池，大小數十戰，不利，諸將失期，士卒困乏。

translations.literal: Wang Chao and Fan Tingzhao encountered him at Wubai Pool; in several dozen battles large and small they fared ill, the generals missed their rendezvous, and the soldiers were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chao and Fan Tingzhao met him at Wubai Pool and fought several dozen engagements, large and small, without success. The generals missed their rendezvous and the troops were worn out.

sentences.zh: 繼遷復令軍主史不癿駐屯橐駝口以阻歸宋人，繼隆遣田敏等擊之。

translations.literal: Jiqian again ordered army master Shi Bufei to station at Camel Pass to block those returning to Song; Jilong dispatched Tian Min and others to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqian posted army master Shi Bufei at Camel Pass to block the Song retreat. Jilong sent Tian Min and others to attack him.

sentences.zh: 咸平春，繼遷復表歸順。

translations.literal: In the spring of Xianping, Jiqian again submitted a memorial of submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the Xianping era Jiqian submitted again, professing loyalty.

sentences.zh: 真宗乃授夏州刺史、定難軍節度、夏銀綏宥靜等州觀察處置押蕃落等使，加邑千戶，實封二百戶，益功臣號，乃放張浦還。

translations.literal: Zhenzong then invested him as prefect of Xia, military commissioner of Dingnan Army, observation and disposition commissioner of Xia, Yin, Sui, You, Jing and other prefectures and commissioner of tribal peoples, adding a thousand fief households and two hundred actual fief households, increasing his merit title, and then released Zhang Pu to return.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong then invested him as prefect of Xia and military commissioner of the Dingnan Army, with authority over Xia, Yin, Sui, You, Jing and neighboring prefectures as commissioner of tribal affairs, added a thousand nominal and two hundred actual fief households, augmented his merit title, and released Zhang Pu to return home.

sentences.zh: 復遣押衙劉仁謙表讓恩命，詔不允，賜仁謙錦袍、銀帶。

translations.literal: He again sent military instructor Liu Renqian with a memorial declining the grace; an edict did not permit it and bestowed on Renqian a brocade robe and silver belt.
translations.idiomatic: He sent military instructor Liu Renqian with a memorial declining the honors; the court refused and rewarded Renqian with a brocade robe and silver belt.

sentences.zh: 尋遣弟繼瑗來謝恩，授繼瑗亳州防禦使，封繼遷母衛慕氏衛國太夫人，子德明爲定難軍節度行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Soon he sent his younger brother Jiyuan to express thanks; Jiyuan was invested defensive commissioner of Bozhou, Jiqian's mother Lady Wei of the Weimo clan was enfeoffed Grand Madam of the State of Wei, and his son Deming was made army marshal of the Dingnan Army military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he sent his brother Jiyuan to give thanks. Jiyuan was made defensive commissioner of Bozhou; Jiqian's mother, Lady Wei of the Weimo clan, was enfeoffed Grand Madam of Wei; and his son Deming was appointed army marshal under the Dingnan commission.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復抄邊。

translations.literal: Before long he again raided the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was raiding the border again.

sentences.zh: 四年，麟府副部署曹璨率熟戶兵邀繼遷輜重于柳撥川，殺獲甚衆。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Deputy Commander of Lin and Fu Cao Shen led allied tribesmen to intercept Jiqian's baggage train at Liubo River, killing and capturing many.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Deputy Commander Cao Shen of Lin and Fu led allied tribesmen in an ambush of Jiqian's supply train at Liubo River, inflicting heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 九月，來攻破定州、懷遠縣及堡靜、永州，清遠軍監軍段義叛，城遂陷。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he came and stormed Ding Prefecture, Huaiyuan County, and Baojing and Yong Prefectures; Qingyuan Army supervisor Duan Yi rebelled and the city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he attacked and captured Ding Prefecture, Huaiyuan County, and the prefectures of Baojing and Yong. Duan Yi, military supervisor of Qingyuan Army, defected, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，繼遷大集蕃部，攻陷靈州，以爲西平府。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year Jiqian greatly assembled tribal forces, captured Ling Prefecture, and made it Xiping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year Jiqian mustered his tribal forces, took Ling Prefecture, and made it his capital of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 六年春，遂都于靈州，詔遣張崇貴、王涉議和，割河西銀、夏等五州與之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year he then made his capital at Ling Prefecture; an edict dispatched Zhang Chonggui and Wang She to negotiate peace, ceding the five Hexi prefectures Yin, Xia, and others to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year he established his capital at Ling Prefecture. The court sent Zhang Chonggui and Wang She to negotiate peace and cede five Hexi prefectures including Yin and Xia.

sentences.zh: 六月，復以二萬騎圍麟州，詔金明巡檢李繼周擊之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he again with twenty thousand cavalry besieged Lin Prefecture; an edict ordered Jinming Inspector Li Jizhou to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he besieged Lin Prefecture with twenty thousand cavalry. The court ordered Jinming Inspector Li Jizhou to strike him.

sentences.zh: 圍未解，麟州部署請濟師，真宗閱地圖曰：「麟州依險，三面孤絕，戮力可守，但城中乏水可憂耳。

translations.literal: Before the siege was lifted, the Lin Prefecture commander requested reinforcements; Zhenzong, examining the map, said: "Lin Prefecture relies on terrain; on three sides it is isolated and impassable—with united effort it can be held, but the lack of water within the city is worrisome."
translations.idiomatic: Before the siege lifted, Lin's commander asked for reinforcements. Zhenzong studied the map and said, "Lin sits on defensible ground, isolated on three sides—it can be held if the garrison stands together, but the shortage of water inside the walls is the real worry."

sentences.zh: 」乃遣兵走援。

translations.literal: He then dispatched troops to hurry to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were dispatched at once to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 繼遷果據水砦，薄城已五日。

translations.literal: Jiqian indeed seized the water fort and had pressed the city for five days already.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqian had indeed seized the water supply and had been pressing the city for five days.

sentences.zh: 知州衛居寶出奇兵突戰，縋勇士城下，城上鼓噪，矢石如注，殺傷萬餘人，繼遷乃拔去。

translations.literal: Prefect Wei Jubao sent unexpected troops in a sudden attack, lowered brave men down the wall, the city above drummed and shouted, arrows and stones poured like rain, more than ten thousand were killed and wounded, and Jiqian then lifted the siege and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Wei Jubao launched a surprise attack, lowered warriors over the wall, and with drums and shouts from the ramparts and a rain of arrows and stones killed and wounded more than ten thousand. Jiqian then lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 遂率衆攻西蕃，取西涼府，都首領潘羅支偽降，繼遷受之不疑。

translations.literal: He then led his forces to attack the Western Tibetans, seized Xiliang Prefecture; paramount chieftain Pan Luozhi feigned surrender and Jiqian accepted it without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched against the western Tibetans and took Xiliang Prefecture. Paramount chieftain Pan Luozhi feigned submission, and Jiqian accepted it without suspicion.

sentences.zh: 羅支遽集六穀蕃部及者龍族合擊之，繼遷大敗，中流矢。

translations.literal: Luozhi swiftly gathered the Six Valleys tribes and the Zhelong clan to strike him jointly; Jiqian was greatly defeated and was struck by a flying arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhi swiftly rallied the Six Valleys tribes and the Zhelong to attack together. Jiqian was routed and took an arrow wound.

sentences.zh: 八月，復聚兵浦洛河，聲言攻環州，詔張凝等分兵以待之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he again gathered troops at the Pulu River, proclaiming an attack on Huan Prefecture; an edict ordered Zhang Ning and others to divide forces to await him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he massed troops on the Pulu River, claiming he would attack Huan Prefecture. The court ordered Zhang Ning and others to divide their forces in anticipation.

sentences.zh: 景德元年正月二日卒，年四十二，子德明立。

translations.literal: On the second day of the first month of the first year of Jingde he died, aged forty-two; his son Deming succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the first month of the first year of Jingde he died at forty-two. His son Deming succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 祥符五年，德明追上繼遷尊號曰應運法天神智仁聖至道廣德孝光皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xiangfu, Deming posthumously added to Jiqian the honorific title Emperor Yingyun Fatian Senshen Rensheng Zhidao Guangde Xiaoguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xiangfu, Deming posthumously honored Jiqian as Emperor Yingyun Fatian Senshen Rensheng Zhidao Guangde Xiaoguang.

sentences.zh: 元昊追諡曰神武，廟號太祖，墓號裕陵。

translations.literal: Yuanhao posthumously titled him Shenwu, temple name Taizu, tomb name Yuling.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao gave him the posthumous title Shenwu, the temple name Taizu, and the tomb name Yuling.

sentences.zh: 德明小字阿移，母曰順成懿孝皇后野利氏，即位于柩前，時年二十三。

translations.literal: Deming's childhood name was Ayi; his mother was Empress Shuncheng Yixiao of the Yeli clan; he succeeded at the bier, aged twenty-three at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Deming's childhood name was Ayi. His mother was Empress Shuncheng Yixiao of the Yeli clan. He took the throne before his father's coffin at twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 邊臣以德明初立，乞詔撫之，因賜詔令審圖去就。

translations.literal: Frontier officials, because Deming had just succeeded, begged an edict to comfort him; an edict was therefore granted instructing him to weigh carefully whether to stay or go.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials, noting that Deming had only just succeeded, asked the court to reassure him. An edict was issued urging him to weigh his options carefully.

sentences.zh: 又詔蕃族萬山、萬遇、龐羅逝安、萬子都虞候、軍主吳守正馬尾等，能率部下歸順者，授團練使，銀萬兩、絹萬匹、錢五萬緡、茶五千斤；

translations.literal: An edict also [addressed] the tribal peoples Wanshan, Wanyu, Pangluoshi'an, Wanzidu yuhou, army master Wu Shouzheng Mayi, and others: whoever could lead his followers to submit would be appointed regimental trainer, with ten thousand taels of silver, ten thousand bolts of silk, fifty thousand strings of cash, and five thousand jin of tea;
translations.idiomatic: Another edict promised the tribal leaders Wanshan, Wanyu, Pangluoshi'an, Wanzidu yuhou, army master Wu Shouzheng Mayi, and others that whoever brought his followers over would receive the rank of regimental trainer, ten thousand taels of silver, ten thousand bolts of silk, fifty thousand strings of cash, and five thousand jin of tea;

sentences.zh: 其有亡命叛去者，釋罪甄錄。

translations.literal: as for those who had fled as outlaws or rebelled and left, their crimes would be pardoned and they would be selected and enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: and any who had fled or defected would be pardoned and received back into service.

sentences.zh: 既而康奴𡗀移等率屬來降。

translations.literal: Before long Kangnu Xiyi and others led their followers to come and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Kangnu Xiyi and others brought their followers in submission.

sentences.zh: 德明遣牙將王旻奉表歸順，賜旻錦袍、銀帶，遣侍禁夏居厚持詔答之，因詔河西羌族各守疆場。

translations.literal: Deming dispatched tooth general Wang Min with a memorial of submission; Min was bestowed a brocade robe and silver belt, attendant Xia Juhou was dispatched bearing an edict in reply, and thereby an edict [ordered] the Hexi Qiang tribes each to guard their borders.
translations.idiomatic: Deming sent staff officer Wang Min with a memorial professing loyalty. Min was given a brocade robe and silver belt; attendant Xia Juhou was sent with a reply edict, and the Hexi Qiang were ordered to keep to their borders.

sentences.zh: 德明連歲表歸順。

translations.literal: Deming for successive years submitted memorials of submission.
translations.idiomatic: Deming sent memorials of loyalty year after year.

sentences.zh: 三年，復遣牙將劉仁勖奉誓表請藏盟府，且言父有遺命。

translations.literal: In the third year he again sent tooth general Liu Renxu with a sworn memorial requesting that the covenant be deposited in the archives, and moreover stated that his father had a dying charge.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he sent staff officer Liu Renxu with a sworn memorial asking that the covenant be kept in the imperial archives, citing his father's dying wish.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，乃授特進、檢校太師兼侍中、持節都督夏州諸軍事、行夏州刺史、上柱國，充定難軍節度、夏銀綏宥靜等州管內觀察處置押蕃落等使，西平王，食邑六千戶，食實封一千戶，仍賜推忠保順亮節翊戴功臣。

translations.literal: The emperor commended this and invested him as special advanced, honorary grand preceptor concurrently palace attendant, holding staff as area commander of all military affairs of Xia Prefecture, acting prefect of Xia, pillar of state, filling the post of military commissioner of Dingnan Army, observation and disposition commissioner of Xia, Yin, Sui, You, Jing and other prefectures within the circuit and commissioner of tribal peoples, King of Xiping, with a fief of six thousand households and actual fief of one thousand households, and moreover bestowed the merit title Loyalty-Preserving, Submission-Maintaining, Bright-Integrity, Assist-Enthroning Merit Lord.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and invested him as special advanced grandee, honorary grand preceptor and palace attendant, area commander of Xia military affairs and acting prefect of Xia, pillar of state, military commissioner of the Dingnan Army with authority over Xia, Yin, Sui, You, Jing and neighboring prefectures as commissioner of tribal affairs, King of Xiping, with six thousand nominal and one thousand actual fief households, and the merit title Loyalty-Preserving, Submission-Maintaining, Bright-Integrity, Assist-Enthroning Merit Lord.

sentences.zh: 遣內侍左右班都知張崇貴、太常博士趙湘等充旌節官告使，賜襲衣、金帶、銀鞍勒馬、銀萬兩、絹萬匹、錢三萬貫、茶二萬斤，給奉如內地。

translations.literal: He dispatched palace attendant and director of the Left and Right Bans Zhang Chonggui, Doctor of the Grand Sacrifices Zhao Xiang, and others as envoys bearing banners and credentials; bestowed formal robes, gold belt, silver-saddled horse, ten thousand taels of silver, ten thousand bolts of silk, thirty thousand strings of cash, twenty thousand jin of tea; salary granted as in the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonggui, director of the Left and Right Bans, Doctor of the Grand Sacrifices Zhao Xiang, and others were sent as credential-bearers with formal robes, a gold belt, a silver-saddled horse, ten thousand taels of silver, ten thousand bolts of silk, thirty thousand strings of cash, and twenty thousand jin of tea, and his stipend was set equal to officials in the interior.

sentences.zh: 因責子弟入質，德明謂非先世故事，不遣。

translations.literal: He moreover required that sons and younger brothers be sent as hostages; Deming said this was not a precedent of former generations and did not send them.
translations.idiomatic: The court also demanded hostages from among his kin. Deming replied that this was not a precedent of earlier times and refused.

sentences.zh: 乃獻御馬二十五匹、散馬七百匹、橐駝三百頭謝恩。

translations.literal: He then presented twenty-five imperial horses, seven hundred ordinary horses, and three hundred camels to express thanks for the grace.
translations.idiomatic: He sent twenty-five imperial horses, seven hundred ordinary horses, and three hundred camels in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，以天書降，加賜守正功臣，益食邑一千戶，食實封四百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, because the Heavenly Writ descended, he was additionally granted the merit title Righteousness-Maintaining Merit Lord, fief increased by one thousand households, actual fief by four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, when the Heavenly Writ descended, he received the additional merit title Righteousness-Maintaining Merit Lord, plus one thousand nominal and four hundred actual fief households.

sentences.zh: 俄境內旱，詔榷場勿禁西人市糧，以振其乏。

translations.literal: Soon drought afflicted the territory; an edict ordered that at the border markets Western people not be forbidden to buy grain, to relieve their destitution.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck his territory, the court ordered border markets not to bar western peoples from buying grain, to ease their want.

sentences.zh: 東封，又遣使來獻，禮成，加兼中書令，益食邑千戶，實封四百戶。

translations.literal: At the Eastern Mount Tai feng ritual he again sent envoys to present tribute; when the rite was completed he was additionally made concurrently grand councilor, fief increased by a thousand households, actual fief by four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Mount feng sacrifice he sent tribute again. When the rite was complete he was made concurrently grand councilor, with a thousand additional nominal and four hundred actual fief households.

sentences.zh: 時遼亦遣使冊德明爲大夏國王。

translations.literal: At the time Liao also sent envoys to enfeoff Deming as Great King of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao at the same time sent envoys to invest Deming as Great King of Xia.

sentences.zh: 明年，出侵回鶻，恒星晝見，德明懼而還。

translations.literal: The next year he went out to invade the Uyghurs; a fixed star appeared in daylight; Deming feared and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he marched against the Uyghurs. A star appeared in daylight; Deming took it as an omen and turned back.

sentences.zh: 三年，境內饑，上表求粟百萬，朝議不知所出。

translations.literal: In the third year famine afflicted the territory; he submitted a memorial requesting a million [units] of grain; court deliberation did not know whence to obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year famine struck his realm. He asked for a million measures of grain, and the court could not see where to find it.

sentences.zh: 時王旦爲相，請敕有司具粟百萬于京師，詔其來取。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Dan was chancellor; he requested an edict that the relevant offices prepare a million [units] of grain at the capital and an edict that he come to fetch it.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Wang Dan proposed that the relevant offices prepare a million measures at the capital and that Deming be told to come and take it.

sentences.zh: 德明既得詔，曰：「朝廷有人。

translations.literal: When Deming received the edict he said: "The court has competent men."
translations.idiomatic: When Deming received the edict he said, "The court has men of talent."

sentences.zh: 」遂止。

translations.literal: He then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: And he dropped the request.

sentences.zh: 大起宮室于𨫼子山。

translations.literal: He greatly raised palace halls on Tuanzi Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He undertook a major building program on Tuanzi Mountain.

sentences.zh: 會旱，西攻河州、甘州宗哥族及秦州緣邊熟戶。

translations.literal: Encountering drought, he attacked westward He Prefecture, the Zongge clan of Gan Prefecture, and the allied tribes on the borders of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck, he marched west against He Prefecture, the Zongge clan of Gan Prefecture, and the allied tribes on the Qin frontier.

sentences.zh: 遂出大里河，築柵蒼耳平。

translations.literal: He then went out to the Dali River and built a stockade at Cangerping.
translations.idiomatic: He then advanced to the Dali River and built a stockade at Cangerping.

sentences.zh: 四年，祀汾陰，進中書令。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, at the sacrifice to Fenyin, he was promoted to grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, at the Fenyin sacrifice, he was promoted to grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 五年，聖祖降，加守太保。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when the Holy Ancestor descended, he was additionally granted as guardian grand mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when the Holy Ancestor descended, he was made guardian grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，謁太清宮，遣使來獻方物，加宣德功臣。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year, at the visit to the Grand Pure Palace, he sent envoys to present local products; he was granted the merit title Virtue-Proclaiming Merit Lord.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year, when the emperor visited the Grand Pure Palace, Deming sent tribute and received the merit title Virtue-Proclaiming Merit Lord.

sentences.zh: 八年，築堡于石州濁輪穀，將建榷場，詔緣邊安撫司止之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he built a fort at Zhuolun Valley in Shi Prefecture, intending to establish a border market; an edict ordered the frontier pacification office to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he built a fort at Zhuolun Valley in Shi Prefecture, planning a border market. The frontier pacification office was ordered to prevent it.

sentences.zh: 九年，因表邊臣違約招納逃亡，云：「自景德中進誓表，朝廷亦降詔書，應兩地逃民，緣邊雜戶不令停舍，皆俾交還。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, by memorial he reported that frontier officials had violated the covenant by enticing and accepting fugitives, saying: "Since the sworn memorial submitted in Jingde and the edict the court also issued, concerning fugitive people of both lands, mixed households on the border were not permitted to harbor them—all were to be mutually returned."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he memorialized that frontier officials were violating the treaty by sheltering fugitives, writing: "Since I submitted the sworn memorial in the Jingde era and the court issued its edict in reply, fugitives from either side and mixed frontier households were not to be given shelter—all were to be handed back."

sentences.zh: 自茲謹守翰垣，頗有倫理。

translations.literal: From then I have strictly guarded the border barriers and there has been considerable order.
translations.idiomatic: "Since then both sides have kept the border with some propriety."

sentences.zh: 自向敏中歸闕，張崇貴雲亡，後來邊臣，罕守舊制，各務邀功，不虞生事，遂致綏、延等界，涇、原以來，擅舉兵甲，入臣境土；

translations.literal: Since Xiang Minzhong returned to court and Zhang Chonggui passed away, the frontier officials who came after rarely maintained the old regulations; each sought merit, without anticipating creating incidents, so that on the borders of Sui, Yan, and others, from Jing and Yuan onward, they unilaterally raised arms and entered my territory;
translations.idiomatic: "Since Xiang Minzhong returned to court and Zhang Chonggui died, later frontier officials have rarely kept the old rules. Each seeks glory without regard for provoking trouble. On the Sui and Yan frontiers and from Jing and Yuan westward, they have taken up arms on their own authority and entered my territory;"

sentences.zh: 其有叛亡部族，劫掠主財，去者百無十回。

translations.literal: as for defecting and fleeing tribal groups, plundering my subjects' property, of those who leave not one in ten returns.
translations.idiomatic: "and of defectors who raid my people's goods, fewer than one in ten ever come back."

sentences.zh: 臣之邊吏，亦務蔽藏，俱失奏論，漸棄盟約。

translations.literal: My frontier officials also strive to conceal them; both sides fail to report and discuss, gradually abandoning the covenant.
translations.idiomatic: "My own border officers conceal them as well. Neither side reports the truth, and the covenant is being cast aside."

sentences.zh: 」詔答已令鄜延、涇原、環慶、麟府等路約束邊部，毋相攻劫，其有隱蔽逃亡，畫時勘送。

translations.literal: The edict in reply stated that it had already ordered the Bian-Yan, Jing-Yuan, Huan-Qing, Lin-Fu and other circuits to restrain the frontier tribes, not to attack and raid each other; as for those who conceal fugitives, they are to be investigated and sent back at once.
translations.idiomatic: The reply edict stated that the Bian-Yan, Jing-Yuan, Huan-Qing, Lin-Fu, and other frontier commands had been ordered to restrain their border populations from mutual raids, and that any who sheltered fugitives must investigate and return them immediately.

sentences.zh: 本國亦宜戒部下，毋有藏匿，各遵紀律，以守封疆。

translations.literal: Our state too should admonish its subordinates not to harbor anyone, each observe discipline, and thereby guard the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Deming's state was also to warn its people against harboring fugitives and to keep discipline and guard the frontier.

sentences.zh: 五年，德明追尊繼遷爲太祖應運法天神智仁聖至道廣德光孝皇帝，廟號武宗。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Deming posthumously honored Jiqian as Emperor Taizu Yingyun Fatian Senshen Rensheng Zhidao Guangde Guangxiao, temple name Wuzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Deming posthumously honored Jiqian as Emperor Taizu Yingyun Fatian Senshen Rensheng Zhidao Guangde Guangxiao, with the temple name Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 七年，甘露降國中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year sweet dew descended within the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year sweet dew fell across the realm.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年正月，加守太傅，食邑千戶，實封四百戶。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Tianxi he was additionally granted as guardian grand tutor, fief a thousand households, actual fief four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Tianxi he was made guardian grand tutor, with one thousand additional nominal and four hundred actual fief households.

sentences.zh: 三年春，德明丁繼立母憂，除起復如前制，以屯田員外郎上官亻必爲吊贈兼起復官告使，閣門祗候常希古爲致祭使。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year Deming entered mourning for the founding mother; exemption and recall to office followed the previous regulation; Field Officer Second Rank Shangguan Bi was made envoy for condolences, posthumous gifts, and recall credentials, and Gate Usher Chang Xigu was made envoy for presenting sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year Deming entered mourning for his mother. He was recalled to office under the usual regulations. Field Officer Second Rank Shangguan Bi was sent as envoy for condolences, posthumous gifts, and recall credentials, and Gate Usher Chang Xigu as envoy to present sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 冬，郊祀，又加崇仁功臣。

translations.literal: In winter, at the suburban sacrifice, he was additionally granted the merit title Respect-Benevolence Merit Lord.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, at the suburban sacrifice, he received the merit title Respect-Benevolence Merit Lord.

sentences.zh: 四年，遼主親將兵五十萬，以狩爲言，來攻涼甸，德明帥衆逆拒，敗之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Liao ruler personally led five hundred thousand troops, claiming it was a hunt, to attack the Liang region; Deming commanded his forces to oppose and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Liao emperor personally led five hundred thousand men, claiming a hunting expedition, to attack the Liang region. Deming met him in force and routed him.

sentences.zh: 五年，遼復遣金吾衛上將軍蕭孝誠齎玉冊金印，冊爲尚書令、大夏國王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Liao again dispatched General-in-Chief of the Golden Quarters Guard Xiao Xiaocheng bearing jade patent and gold seal to enfeoff him as Director of the Department of State Affairs and Great King of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Liao sent General-in-Chief of the Golden Quarters Guard Xiao Xiaocheng with a jade patent and gold seal to invest him as Director of the Department of State Affairs and Great King of Xia.

sentences.zh: 乾興元年，加純誠功臣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianxing he was granted the merit title Pure-Sincerity Merit Lord.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianxing he received the merit title Pure-Sincerity Merit Lord.

sentences.zh: 德明自歸順以來，每歲旦、聖節、冬至皆遣牙校來獻不絕。

translations.literal: Since Deming's submission, every New Year's dawn, imperial birthday, and winter solstice he without cease dispatched staff officers to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Since submitting to the Song, Deming sent staff officers with tribute every New Year, imperial birthday, and winter solstice without fail.

sentences.zh: 而每加恩賜官告，則又以襲衣五，金荔支帶、金花銀匣副之，銀沙鑼、盆、合千兩，錦彩千匹，金塗銀鞍勒馬一匹，副以纓、復，遣內臣就賜之。

translations.literal: And whenever grace was added with an appointment patent, there were moreover five formal robes, gold lychee-branch belt, gold-flower silver box as complement, a thousand taels of silver sand gongs, basins, and boxes, a thousand bolts of brocade silk, one gold-plated silver-saddled horse, complemented with bridle ornaments and covers; palace attendants were dispatched to grant them on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever new honors came with appointment patents, the court also sent five formal robes, a gold lychee-branch belt, a gold-flower silver casket, a thousand taels of silver in gongs, basins, and boxes, a thousand bolts of brocade, a gold-plated silver-saddled horse with full tack, delivered by palace envoys.

sentences.zh: 又遣閣門祗候賜冬服及頒《儀天具注曆》。

translations.literal: Gate ushers were again dispatched to bestow winter garments and distribute the "Yitian Annotated Calendar."
translations.idiomatic: Gate ushers were also sent with winter clothing and copies of the Yitian Annotated Calendar.

sentences.zh: 明年，攻慶州柔遠砦。

translations.literal: The next year he attacked Rouyuan Stockade in Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he attacked Rouyuan Stockade in Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 巡檢楊承吉與戰不利，命曹瑋爲環、慶、秦州緣邊巡檢安撫使禦備之。

translations.literal: Inspector Yang Chengji fought and fared ill; Cao Wei was appointed frontier inspector and pacification commissioner of Huan, Qing, and Qin to defend against him.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Yang Chengji was beaten in the fight. Cao Wei was made frontier inspector and pacification commissioner for Huan, Qing, and Qin to meet the threat.

sentences.zh: 德明城懷遠鎮爲興州以居。

translations.literal: Deming fortified Huaiyuan Town as Xing Prefecture to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Deming fortified Huaiyuan into Xing Prefecture and made it his seat.

sentences.zh: 天聖六年，德明遣子元昊攻甘州，拔之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tiansheng, Deming dispatched his son Yuanhao to attack Gan Prefecture and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tiansheng Deming sent his son Yuanhao against Gan Prefecture and took it.

sentences.zh: 八年，瓜州王以千騎降于夏。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Prince of Guazhou with a thousand cavalry submitted to Xia.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the lord of Guazhou surrendered to Xia with a thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 火星入南斗。

translations.literal: Mars entered Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Mars entered the constellation of the Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 九年十月，德明卒，時年五十一，追諡曰光聖皇帝，廟號太宗，墓號嘉陵。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the ninth year Deming died, aged fifty-one; posthumously honored as Emperor Guang Sheng, temple name Taizong, tomb name Jialing.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the ninth year Deming died at fifty-one. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Emperor Guang Sheng, with temple name Taizong and tomb name Jialing.

sentences.zh: 宋贈太師、尚書令兼中書令，以尚書度支員外郎朱昌符爲祭奠使，六宅副使、內侍省內侍押班馮仁俊副之，賻絹七百匹、布三百匹，副以上醞、羊、米、面。
