translations.literal: Song posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, Director of the Department of State Affairs concurrently Palace Secretariat Director; appointed Zhu Changfu, outer-office member of the Revenue Bureau of the Department of State Affairs, as condolence envoy, with Feng Renjun, deputy commissioner of the Six Residences and inner-palace rank officer of the Palace Domestic Service, as assistant; funeral gifts of seven hundred bolts of silk and three hundred bolts of cloth, complemented with fine wine, sheep, rice, and flour.
translations.idiomatic: The Song posthumously granted him Grand Preceptor, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Director of the Secretariat. Zhu Changfu of the Revenue Bureau was sent as condolence envoy, assisted by Feng Renjun of the Palace Domestic Service. The court gave seven hundred bolts of silk and three hundred of cloth for the obsequies, with fine wine, sheep, rice, and flour besides.

sentences.zh: 將葬，賜物稱是，皇太后所賜亦如之。

translations.literal: When the burial was imminent, gifts were granted commensurately; what the Empress Dowager bestowed was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: As burial approached, the court gave commensurate gifts, and the Empress Dowager's presents matched them.

sentences.zh: 帝與皇太后成服于苑中。

translations.literal: The Emperor and Empress Dowager put on mourning dress in the palace garden.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor and Empress Dowager donned mourning garb in the palace garden.

sentences.zh: 子曩霄立。

translations.literal: His son Nangxiao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Nangxiao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 曩霄本名元昊，小字嵬理，國語謂惜爲「嵬」，富貴爲「理」。

translations.literal: Nangxiao's original name was Yuanhao, childhood name Weili; in the national language "cherished" is wei and "wealth and nobility" is li.
translations.idiomatic: Nangxiao's given name was Yuanhao, his childhood name Weili—the national tongue took wei to mean "cherished" and li to mean "noble and prosperous."

sentences.zh: 母曰惠慈敦愛皇后衛慕氏。

translations.literal: His mother was Empress Weici Dun'ai, née Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Empress Weici Dun'ai of the Wei clan.

sentences.zh: 性雄毅，多大略，善繪畫，能創制物始。

translations.literal: By nature bold and resolute, with great strategic vision; skilled at painting and able to originate new things from the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and resolute by nature, he had broad strategic vision, painted well, and could conceive and create things anew.

sentences.zh: 圓面高准，身長五尺餘。

translations.literal: Round face, high nose bridge, body height more than five chi.
translations.idiomatic: He had a round face and prominent nose, and stood more than five chi tall.

sentences.zh: 少時好衣長袖緋衣，冠黑冠，佩弓矢，從衛步卒張青蓋。

translations.literal: In youth he liked wearing long-sleeved scarlet robes, black cap, carrying bow and arrows; foot soldiers of his guard spread a green canopy.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he favored long-sleeved scarlet robes, a black cap, bow and arrows at his belt, with foot guards holding a green canopy over him.

sentences.zh: 出乘馬，以二旗引，百餘騎自從。

translations.literal: When going out he rode a horse, two banners leading, more than a hundred mounted followers attending him.
translations.idiomatic: Abroad he rode with two banners going before and more than a hundred mounted men in his train.

sentences.zh: 曉浮圖學，通蕃漢文字，案上置法律，常攜《野戰歌》、《太乙金鑒訣》。

translations.literal: He understood Buddhist learning, mastered both Tangut and Chinese script; legal codes on his desk, he usually carried "Song of Field Combat" and "Golden Mirror Secrets of Taiyi."
translations.idiomatic: He knew Buddhist learning and both Tangut and Chinese writing. Legal codes lay on his desk, and he often carried the Song of Field Combat and the Golden Mirror Secrets of Taiyi.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，獨引兵襲破回鶻夜洛隔可汗王，奪甘州，遂立爲皇太子。

translations.literal: At coming of age he alone led troops in a surprise attack that broke Uyghur Qaghan Yeluoge, seized Gan Prefecture, and was thereupon established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: At his coming of age he personally led a raid that shattered the Uyghur qaghan Yeluoge, seized Gan Prefecture, and was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 數諫其父毋臣宋，父輒戒之曰：「吾久用兵，疲矣。

translations.literal: He repeatedly admonished his father not to serve as subject to Song; his father would warn him, saying: "I have long used arms and am weary."
translations.idiomatic: He often urged his father to stop serving the Song as a vassal. Deming would always warn him: "I have fought for years and am worn out."

sentences.zh: 吾族三十年衣錦綺，此宋恩也，不可負。

translations.literal: Our clan for thirty years has worn brocade and fine silk—this is Song grace; it must not be betrayed.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years our people have worn brocade and fine silk—that is Song favor, and we must not betray it."

sentences.zh: 」元昊曰：「衣皮毛，事畜牧，蕃性所便。

translations.literal: Yuanhao said: "Wearing fur and leather, tending livestock—that is what suits the frontier nature.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao replied: "Furs and hides, tending herds—that is what a frontier people do best.

sentences.zh: 英雄之生，當王霸耳，何錦綺爲？

translations.literal: When heroes are born, they should rule as kings and hegemons—what need is there for brocade and fine silk?
translations.idiomatic: A true hero is born to reign as king or hegemon—what need has he for brocade?"

sentences.zh: 」德明卒，即授特進、檢校太師兼侍中、定難軍節度、夏銀綏宥靜等州觀察處置押蕃落使、西平王，以工部郎中楊告爲旌節官告使，禮賓副使朱允中副之。

translations.literal: When Deming died, Yuanhao was immediately granted Special Advancement, Acting Grand Preceptor concurrently Palace Attendant, military commissioner of the Dingnan Army, observation and disposition commissioner for Xia, Yin, Sui, You, and Jing and frontier tribal commissioner, and King of Xiping; Yang Gao of the Ministry of Works was made credentialed appointment envoy, with Vice Commissioner of Ceremonial Reception Zhu Yunzhong as assistant.
translations.idiomatic: After Deming's death the court at once confirmed Yuanhao as Special Advancement, Acting Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant, military commissioner of the Dingnan Army, observation and disposition commissioner over Xia, Yin, Sui, You, and Jing with charge of frontier tribes, and King of Xiping. Yang Gao of the Ministry of Works carried the appointment patent as envoy, assisted by Zhu Yunzhong of Ceremonial Reception.

sentences.zh: 既襲封，明號令，以兵法勒諸部。

translations.literal: Once he had inherited the fief, he clarified commands and regulations and governed the various tribes by military law.
translations.idiomatic: After succeeding to the fief he tightened command and governed the tribes by military discipline.

sentences.zh: 始衣白窄衫，氈冠紅裏，冠頂後垂紅結綬，自號嵬名吾祖。

translations.literal: He first wore a white narrow robe, felt cap with red lining, red knotted ribbon hanging from the back of the cap crown, and styled himself Weiming Wuzu.
translations.idiomatic: He now wore a white close-fitting robe and a felt cap lined in red, with a red knotted cord hanging from the back of the crown, and took the style Weiming Wuzu.

sentences.zh: 凡六日、九日則見官屬。

translations.literal: On every sixth and ninth day he received officials.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth and ninth of each month he held audience with his officials.

sentences.zh: 其官分文武班，曰中書，曰樞密，曰三司，曰御史台，曰開封府，曰翊衛司，曰官計司，曰受納司，曰農田司，曰群牧司，曰飛龍院，曰磨勘司，曰文思院，曰蕃學，曰漢學。

translations.literal: His offices divided civil and military ranks, called Secretariat, Bureau of Military Affairs, Three Departments, Censorate, Kaifeng Prefecture, Guard Bureau, Fiscal Bureau, Receipt Bureau, Agriculture Bureau, Herds Bureau, Flying Dragon Court, Review Bureau, Literary Craft Court, Tangut College, and Han College.
translations.idiomatic: His government divided civil and military service into a Secretariat, Bureau of Military Affairs, Three Departments, Censorate, Kaifeng Prefecture, Guard Bureau, Fiscal Bureau, Receipt Bureau, Agriculture Bureau, Herds Bureau, Flying Dragon Court, Review Bureau, Literary Craft Court, Tangut College, and Han College.

sentences.zh: 自中書令、宰相、樞使、大夫、侍中、太尉已下，皆分命蕃漢人爲之。

translations.literal: From Secretariat Director, chancellor, commissioner of military affairs, grand counselor, palace attendant, and grand marshal downward, all were separately appointed among Tangut and Han persons.
translations.idiomatic: From Secretariat Director, chancellor, military commissioner, grand counselor, palace attendant, and grand marshal on down, Tangut and Han men were appointed in turn.

sentences.zh: 文資則襆頭、鞾笏、紫衣、緋衣；

translations.literal: Civil posts wore putou headgear, boots and tablet, purple robes, and scarlet robes;
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials wore putou caps, boots and court tablets, and purple or scarlet robes;

sentences.zh: 武職則冠金帖起雲鏤冠、銀帖間金縷冠、黑漆冠，衣紫旋襽，金塗銀束帶，垂蹀躞，佩解結錐、短刀、弓矢韣，馬乘鯢皮鞍，垂紅纓，打跨鈸拂。

translations.literal: Military posts wore gold-inlaid cloud-pattern filigree cap, silver-inlaid gold-thread cap, or black lacquer cap; wore purple round-collared robes, gold-plated silver belt, dangling diexie ornaments, carrying knot-releasing awl, short knife, and bow-and-arrow case; horses bore crocodile-skin saddles with red tassels, and they struck bridle pommel cymbals.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers wore gold-inlaid cloud-scroll caps, silver-inlaid gold-thread caps, or black lacquer caps, with purple round-collared gowns, gold-plated silver belts and dangling belt plaques, knot-awls, short knives, and quivers at the hip. Their mounts had crocodile-skin saddles with red tassels, and they beat pommel cymbals as they rode.

sentences.zh: 便服則紫皂地繡盤球子花旋襽，束帶。

translations.literal: Everyday dress was purple-black ground embroidered ball-flower round-collared robes, with belt.
translations.idiomatic: Informal dress was a purple-black round-collared robe embroidered with ball-flower patterns, with belt.

sentences.zh: 民庶青綠，以別貴賤。

translations.literal: Commoners wore blue-green to distinguish high and low.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners wore blue-green clothing to mark their rank apart from the elite.

sentences.zh: 每舉兵，必率部長與獵，有獲，則下馬環坐飲，割鮮而食，各問所見，擇取其長。

translations.literal: Whenever he mobilized troops he always led tribal chiefs in hunting; when there was game they dismounted, sat in a circle to drink, cut fresh meat and ate, each asking what the others had observed and selecting the best counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Before every campaign he led the tribal chiefs on a hunt. When game was taken they dismounted, sat in a ring to drink, carved fresh meat, and each gave his counsel—the best was chosen.

sentences.zh: 初，宋改元明道，元昊避父諱，稱顯道于國中。

translations.literal: At first when Song changed the era name to Mingdao, Yuanhao, avoiding his father's taboo, called it Xiandao within his state.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song changed the era name to Mingdao, Yuanhao avoided his father's taboo and used Xiandao at home.

sentences.zh: 二年，加兼中書令。

translations.literal: In the second year he was additionally made concurrent Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was also made concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遣其令公蘇奴兒將兵二萬五千攻唃廝囉，敗死略盡，蘇奴兒被執。

translations.literal: He dispatched his commandery duke Sunu'er leading twenty-five thousand troops to attack Gusiluo; they were defeated and nearly all killed, and Sunu'er was captured.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his commandery duke Sunu'er with twenty-five thousand men against Gusiluo. The force was destroyed almost to the last man, and Sunu'er was taken.

sentences.zh: 元昊自率衆攻貓牛城，一月不下。

translations.literal: Yuanhao personally led the host to attack Mao Niu City; after a month it would not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao personally besieged Mao Niu City, but it did not fall within a month.

sentences.zh: 既而詐約和，城開，乃大縱殺戮。

translations.literal: Then he feigned an offer of peace; when the city opened, he unleashed great slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: He then pretended to sue for peace; when the gates opened he massacred the population.

sentences.zh: 又攻青唐、安二、宗哥、帶星嶺諸城，唃廝囉部將安子羅以兵絕歸路，元昊晝夜角戰二百餘日，子羅敗，遂取瓜、沙、肅三州。

translations.literal: He again attacked Qingtang, An'er, Zongge, Taixingling, and other cities; Gusiluo's officer An Ziluo cut off the return route with troops; Yuanhao fought day and night for more than two hundred days; Ziluo was defeated, and he then took the three prefectures of Gua, Sha, and Su.
translations.idiomatic: He next attacked Qingtang, An'er, Zongge, Taixingling, and other towns. Gusiluo's officer An Ziluo blocked his retreat, and Yuanhao fought night and day for more than two hundred days before Ziluo fell. He then seized Gua, Sha, and Su.

sentences.zh: 元昊既還，欲南侵，恐唃廝囉制其後，復舉兵攻蘭州諸羌，侵至馬銜山，築城凡川。

translations.literal: Yuanhao having returned, wishing to invade south, fearing Gusiluo would check him from behind, again raised troops to attack the various Qiang of Lan Prefecture, penetrated to Maxian Mountain, and built a fortified city at Fanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home Yuanhao planned a southern invasion but feared Gusiluo would strike from behind. He marched again against the Qiang around Lan Prefecture, raided as far as Maxian Mountain, and built a fort at Fanchuan.

sentences.zh: 元昊既悉有夏、銀、綏、宥、靜、靈、鹽、會、勝、甘、涼、瓜、沙、肅，而洪、定、威、龍皆即堡鎮號州，仍居興州，阻河依賀蘭山爲固。

translations.literal: Yuanhao now wholly possessed Xia, Yin, Sui, You, Jing, Ling, Yan, Hui, Sheng, Gan, Liang, Gua, Sha, and Su; Hong, Ding, Wei, and Long were all titled from fortified towns as prefectures; he still dwelt at Xing Prefecture, taking the river as barrier and relying on Helan Mountain for solidity.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao now held Xia, Yin, Sui, You, Jing, Ling, Yan, Hui, Sheng, Gan, Liang, Gua, Sha, and Su. Hong, Ding, Wei, and Long were raised from fortified posts into prefectures. He kept his seat at Xing Prefecture, using the Yellow River and Helan Mountains as his ramparts.

sentences.zh: 始大建官，以嵬名守全、張陟、張絳、楊廓、徐敏宗、張文顯輩主謀議，以鐘鼎臣典文書，以成逋、克成賞、都臥、𡗀如定、多多馬竇、惟吉主兵馬，野利仁榮主蕃學。

translations.literal: He then greatly expanded government, with Weiming Shouquan, Zhang Zhi, Zhang Jiang, Yang Kuo, Xu Minzong, Zhang Wenxian and the like directing counsel; Zhong Dingchen supervised documents; Cheng Bu, Kecheng Shang, Du Wo, Ruoding, Duoduoma Dou, and Weiji commanded troops and horses; Yeli Renrong directed the Tangut College.
translations.idiomatic: He then greatly expanded the bureaucracy. Weiming Shouquan, Zhang Zhi, Zhang Jiang, Yang Kuo, Xu Minzong, and Zhang Wenxian led strategy; Zhong Dingchen kept the archives; Cheng Bu, Kecheng Shang, Du Wo, Ruoding, Duoduoma Dou, and Weiji commanded the armies; Yeli Renrong ran the Tangut College.

sentences.zh: 置十二監軍司，委豪右分統其衆。

translations.literal: He established twelve military supervision commissions and entrusted powerful local families to command their followers in separate divisions.
translations.idiomatic: He set up twelve frontier supervisory commands and entrusted powerful clan leaders to command their followers in turn.

sentences.zh: 自河北至午臘蒻山七萬人，以備契丹；

translations.literal: From north of the Yellow River to Mount Wula Ruoshan, seventy thousand men to guard against Khitan;
translations.idiomatic: Seventy thousand from north of the Yellow River to Mount Wula Ruoshan to guard against the Khitan;

sentences.zh: 河南洪州、白豹、安鹽州、羅落、天都、惟精山等五萬人，以備環、慶、鎮戎、原州；

translations.literal: South of the river at Hong Prefecture, Baibao, Anyan Prefecture, Luoluo, Tiandu, Weijingshan, and the like, fifty thousand men to guard against Huan, Qing, Zhenrong, and Yuan;
translations.idiomatic: Fifty thousand at Hong Prefecture, Baibao, Anyan, Luoluo, Tiandu, Weijingshan, and related posts south of the river against Huan, Qing, Zhenrong, and Yuan;

sentences.zh: 左廂宥州路五萬人，以備鄜、延、麟、府；

translations.literal: Left wing Youzhou route fifty thousand men to guard against Fu, Yan, Lin, and Fu;
translations.idiomatic: Fifty thousand on the left Youzhou route against Fu, Yan, Lin, and Fu;

sentences.zh: 右廂甘州路三萬人，以備西蕃、回紇；

translations.literal: Right wing Ganzhou route thirty thousand men to guard against Tibetans and Uyghurs;
translations.idiomatic: Thirty thousand on the right Gan Prefecture route against Tibetans and Uyghurs;

sentences.zh: 賀蘭駐兵五萬、靈州五萬人、興州興慶府七萬人爲鎮守，總五十余萬。

translations.literal: Helan garrison troops fifty thousand, Ling Prefecture fifty thousand, Xing Prefecture and Xingqingfu seventy thousand as garrison forces—in all more than five hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty thousand at Helan, fifty thousand at Ling Prefecture, and seventy thousand at Xing Prefecture and Xingqingfu as garrisons—more than half a million in all.

sentences.zh: 而苦戰倚山訛，山訛者，橫山羌，平夏兵不及也。

translations.literal: Yet the fiercest fighters relied on Shan'e; Shan'e were the Hengshan Qiang, whom the Pingxia troops could not match.
translations.idiomatic: His hardest fighters were the Shan'e—Hengshan Qiang whom even Pingxia soldiers could not best.

sentences.zh: 選豪族善弓馬五千人迭直，號六班直，月給米二石。

translations.literal: He selected five thousand men of powerful clans skilled at bow and horse for rotating duty, styled the Six-Ban Direct Guard, each month given two shi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand bowmen and riders from powerful clans were drafted in rotation as the Six-Ban Direct Guard, each man receiving two shi of rice monthly.

sentences.zh: 鐵騎三千，分十部。

translations.literal: Iron cavalry three thousand, divided into ten sections.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand iron cavalry were organized in ten divisions.

sentences.zh: 發兵以銀牌召部長面受約束。

translations.literal: To mobilize troops he summoned tribal chiefs with silver plaques to receive commands in person.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were raised by summoning tribal chiefs with silver plaques to receive orders face to face.

sentences.zh: 設十六司于興州，以總庶務。

translations.literal: He established sixteen offices at Xing Prefecture to oversee general affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen administrative offices at Xing Prefecture oversaw all government business.

sentences.zh: 元昊自製蕃書，命野利仁榮演繹之，成十二卷，字形體方整類八分，而畫頗重復。

translations.literal: Yuanhao himself devised the Tangut script and ordered Yeli Renrong to develop it; it formed twelve volumes, the character forms square and regular resembling clerical script, yet strokes were rather repetitive.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao invented a Tangut script and had Yeli Renrong develop it into twelve volumes. The characters were square and regular, like clerical script, though many strokes repeated.

sentences.zh: 教國人紀事用蕃書，而譯《孝經》、《爾雅》、《四言雜字》爲蕃語。

translations.literal: He taught the people to record affairs in Tangut script, and translated the Classic of Filial Piety, Erya, and Four-Character Miscellaneous Words into Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: He taught his people to keep records in Tangut and had the Classic of Filial Piety, Erya, and Four-Character Miscellaneous Words rendered into the Tangut tongue.

sentences.zh: 復改元大慶。

translations.literal: He again changed the era name to Daqing.
translations.idiomatic: He changed the era name again to Daqing.

sentences.zh: 明年，遣使上表曰：

translations.literal: The next year he dispatched envoys submitting a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: The following year he sent envoys with a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣祖宗本出帝胄，當東晉之末運，創後魏之初基。

translations.literal: Your subject's ancestors by origin came from the imperial lineage; at the final fortune of Eastern Jin they founded the early foundation of Northern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject's forebears sprang from the imperial line. At the twilight of Eastern Jin they laid the early foundations of Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 遠祖思恭，當唐季率兵拯難，受封賜姓。

translations.literal: Remote ancestor Sigong, at the end of Tang led troops to rescue the realm in crisis, received enfeoffment and a granted surname.
translations.idiomatic: The distant ancestor Sigong, in Tang's dying years, led troops to relieve the realm and received enfeoffment and a surname from the throne.

sentences.zh: 祖繼遷，心知兵要，手握乾符，大舉義旗，悉降諸部。

translations.literal: Grandfather Jiqian, knowing in his heart the essentials of war, holding the mandate in his hand, raised the banner of righteous revolt and made all tribes submit.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jiqian mastered the arts of war, seized Heaven's mandate, raised the banner of righteous revolt, and brought every tribe to submission.

sentences.zh: 臨河五郡，不旋踵而歸；

translations.literal: The five commanderies along the river returned without turning the heel;
translations.idiomatic: Five commanderies along the river fell to him almost at once;

sentences.zh: 沿邊七州，悉差肩而克。

translations.literal: Seven frontier prefectures were all taken shoulder to shoulder.
translations.idiomatic: and seven frontier prefectures were seized one after another.

sentences.zh: 父德明，嗣奉世基，勉從朝命。

translations.literal: Father Deming inherited and preserved the ancestral foundation, striving to follow court orders.
translations.idiomatic: His father Deming inherited that foundation and, however reluctantly, obeyed the court's commands.

sentences.zh: 真王之號，夙感于頒宣；

translations.literal: The title of True King long ago had moved us when it was proclaimed;
translations.idiomatic: The title True King, once proclaimed, had long filled us with gratitude;

sentences.zh: 尺土之封，顯蒙于割裂。

translations.literal: The grant of even a foot of land plainly benefited us from partition.
translations.idiomatic: and even the smallest grant of territory was a clear mark of imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 臣偶以狂斐，制小蕃文字，改大漢衣冠。

translations.literal: Your subject, by rash presumption, devised a petty Tangut script and altered the great Han dress and caps.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject, in rash audacity, devised a Tangut script and cast off the dress of the Great Han.

sentences.zh: 衣冠既就，文字既行，禮樂既張，器用既備，吐蕃、塔塔、張掖、交河，莫不從伏。

translations.literal: Once dress and caps were ready, script established, rites and music deployed, and implements prepared, Tibetans, Tatars, Zhangye, and Jiaohe none failed to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Once regalia, script, rites, music, and tools were all in place, Tibetans, Tatars, Zhangye, and Jiaohe alike bowed in submission.

sentences.zh: 稱王則不喜，朝帝則是從，輻輳屢期，山呼齊舉，伏願一垓之土地，建爲萬乘之邦家。

translations.literal: To be called king displeased; to attend upon the Emperor was what was followed—yet they gathered repeatedly, shouting as one mountain, humbly wishing the land of one gai to be established as a ten-thousand-chariot state and household.
translations.idiomatic: My people were displeased to call me only king yet willing to pay you homage as emperor—but they have gathered again and again, shouting as one, and humbly ask that this vast domain be raised to a sovereign state in its own right.

sentences.zh: 于時再讓靡遑，群集又迫，事不得已，顯而行之。

translations.literal: At that time declining twice left no leisure; the mass assembly pressed again; the matter could not be avoided, and I openly carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: Twice I tried to decline, but my people would not wait. The assembly pressed on, and necessity left no choice—I proclaimed it openly.

sentences.zh: 遂以十月十一日郊壇備禮，爲世祖始文本武興法建禮仁孝皇帝，國稱大夏，年號天授禮法延祚。

translations.literal: Thereupon on the eleventh day of the tenth month at the suburban altar complete rites were performed; he became Emperor Shiwen, establishing law and ritual, benevolent and filial, founding sage of the line; the state was called Great Xia, era name Heavenly Gifted Ritual Law Extended Succession.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh day of the tenth month he performed the full suburban rites and took the title Emperor Shiwen, Establishing Law and Ritual, Benevolent and Filial, founding sage of the line. His state was named Great Xia, with the era Heavenly Gift of Ritual Law and Extended Succession.

sentences.zh: 伏望皇帝陛下，睿哲成人，寬慈及物，許以西郊之地，冊爲南面之君。

translations.literal: Humbly hoping Your Majesty, wise and enlightened in adulthood, generous and merciful to all things, will grant the lands of the western marches and enfeoff us as sovereign of the south.
translations.idiomatic: Humbly I pray that Your Majesty, wise and generous, will recognize our lands in the western marches and invest us as sovereign of the south.

sentences.zh: 敢竭愚庸，常敦歡好。

translations.literal: I dare exhaust my feeble mediocrity and constantly foster cordial good relations.
translations.idiomatic: I pledge my poor service and will ever cultivate goodwill between us.

sentences.zh: 魚來雁往，任傳鄰國之音；

translations.literal: Fish come and geese go—let neighboring states' messages pass freely;
translations.idiomatic: Let envoys pass back and forth as fish and geese, carrying word between our realms;

sentences.zh: 地久天長，永鎮邊方之患。

translations.literal: Earth enduring, heaven long—forever guarding the troubles of the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: and may our peace endure as long as earth and heaven, forever stilling trouble on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 至誠瀝懇，仰俟帝俞。

translations.literal: With utmost sincerity poured forth in earnest petition, I look up awaiting imperial assent.
translations.idiomatic: In utmost sincerity I await Your Majesty's gracious assent.

sentences.zh: 謹遣弩涉俄疾、你斯悶、臥普令濟、嵬崖妳奉表以聞。

translations.literal: Respectfully dispatching Nushe'eji, Nisimén, Wopu Lingji, and Weiyainü to present this memorial for report.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully submitted by envoys Nushe'eji, Nisimén, Wopu Lingji, and Weiyainü.

sentences.zh: 詔削奪官爵、互市，揭榜于邊，募人能擒元昊若斬首獻者，即爲定難軍節度使。

translations.literal: An edict stripped his titles and frontier markets; notices were posted at the border offering recruitment of anyone who could capture Yuanhao or present his severed head, who would immediately become military commissioner of the Dingnan Army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped his titles and shut down border trade. Notices posted on the frontier promised the Dingnan military commission to anyone who captured Yuanhao or brought in his head.

sentences.zh: 又遣賀永年齎嫚書，納旌節及所授敕告置神明匣，留歸孃族而去。

translations.literal: Yuanhao again dispatched He Yongnian bearing an insolent letter, placing the baton, credentials, and granted appointment edicts in the spirit tablet casket, then leaving them with the Guiyang clan and departing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao sent He Yongnian with an insulting letter, placed the baton, credentials, and appointment patents in the spirit casket, left them with the Guiyang clan, and departed.

sentences.zh: 康定元年，環慶路鈐轄高繼隆、知慶州張崇俊攻後橋，而柔遠砦主武英入自北門，拔之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangding, Huanqing circuit intendant Gao Jilong and Qing Prefecture prefect Zhang Chongjun attacked Houqiao, while Rouyuan Stockade commander Wu Ying entered by the north gate and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangding 1, Huanqing intendant Gao Jilong and Qing Prefecture prefect Zhang Chongjun attacked Houqiao while Rouyuan Stockade commander Wu Ying took it through the north gate.

sentences.zh: 未幾，夏人攻金明砦，執都監李士彬父子。

translations.literal: Before long Xia troops attacked Jinming Stockade and seized garrison commander Li Shibin and his son.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xia forces stormed Jinming Stockade and captured garrison commander Li Shibin and his son.

sentences.zh: 破安遠、塞門、永平諸砦，圍延州，設伏三川口，執劉平、石元孫、傅偃、劉發、石遜等。

translations.literal: They broke Anyuan, Saimen, Yongping, and other stockades, besieged Yan Prefecture, set an ambush at Sanchuankou, and captured Liu Ping, Shi Yuansun, Fu Yan, Liu Fa, Shi Xun, and others.
translations.idiomatic: They overran Anyuan, Saimen, Yongping, and other stockades, besieged Yan Prefecture, ambushed the Song at Sanchuankou, and captured Liu Ping, Shi Yuansun, Fu Yan, Liu Fa, Shi Xun, and others.

sentences.zh: 又攻鎮戎軍，敗劉繼宗、李緯兵五千。

translations.literal: They again attacked Zhenrong Army and defeated five thousand troops under Liu Jizong and Li Wei.
translations.idiomatic: They next struck Zhenrong Army and routed five thousand men under Liu Jizong and Li Wei.

sentences.zh: 環慶部署任福入白豹城，焚其積聚，破四十一族。

translations.literal: Huanqing deployment commander Ren Fu entered Baibao City, burned its stores, and broke forty-one clans.
translations.idiomatic: Huanqing deployment commander Ren Fu took Baibao City, burned its stores, and shattered forty-one clans.

sentences.zh: 慶曆元年二月，攻渭州，逼懷遠城。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Qingli he attacked Wei Prefecture and pressed Huaiyuan City.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Qingli 1 he attacked Wei Prefecture and pressed Huaiyuan City.

sentences.zh: 韓琦徼巡邊至高平，盡發鎮戎兵及募勇士得萬人，命行營總管任福等並擊之，都監桑懌爲前鋒，鈐轄朱觀、都監武英繼之。

translations.literal: Han Qi on border inspection tour reached Gaoping, mobilized all Zhenrong troops and recruited brave men to obtain ten thousand, ordered field headquarters commander Ren Fu and others jointly to strike them; garrison commander Sang Yi as vanguard, intendant Zhu Guan and garrison commander Wu Ying following.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi, on a border inspection, reached Gaoping, mustered every man from Zhenrong and recruited volunteers until he had ten thousand, and ordered field commander Ren Fu and others to strike together. Garrison commander Sang Yi led the van, with intendant Zhu Guan and garrison commander Wu Ying behind him.

sentences.zh: 福申令持重，其夕宿三川，夏人已過懷遠東南。

translations.literal: Fu repeated orders to proceed with caution; that evening they encamped at Sanchuan; Xia troops had already passed southeast of Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu ordered his men to stay cautious. That night they camped at Sanchuan while the Xia army had already moved southeast of Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 翌日，諸軍躡其後。

translations.literal: The next day the various armies followed on their trail.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Song columns marched in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 西路巡檢常鼎、劉肅與夏人對壘于張家堡，懌以騎兵趣之。

translations.literal: Western route inspector Chang Ding and Liu Su faced Xia troops in camp at Zhangjiabao; Yi hurried thither with cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Western route inspectors Chang Ding and Liu Su were locked with the Xia at Zhangjiabao, and Yi raced to them with cavalry.

sentences.zh: 福分兵，夕與懌爲一軍，屯好水川。

translations.literal: Fu divided his force; in the evening he and Yi formed one army and encamped at Haoshui River.
translations.idiomatic: Fu split his force. At dusk he and Yi made one column and camped on the Haoshui River.

sentences.zh: 川與能家川隔在隴山外，觀、英爲一軍，屯籠洛川，相離五里。

translations.literal: That stream and Nengjia Stream were separated beyond Long Mountain; Guan and Ying formed one army and encamped at Longluo Stream, five li apart.
translations.idiomatic: The Haoshui and Nengjia streams lay beyond Long Mountain. Guan and Ying formed a second column at Longluo Stream, five li away.

sentences.zh: 期以明日會兵，不使夏人一騎遁，然已陷其伏中矣。

translations.literal: They planned to join forces the next day and not let a single Xia rider escape—yet they had already fallen into an ambush.
translations.idiomatic: They planned to unite the next day and let no Xia rider escape—but they were already walking into an ambush.

sentences.zh: 元昊自將精兵十萬，營于川口，候者言夏人有砦，數不多，兵益進。

translations.literal: Yuanhao personally commanded a hundred thousand elite troops encamped at the river mouth; scouts said the Xia had a camp, not many in number, and the army pressed forward more.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao himself commanded a hundred thousand elite troops at the river mouth. Scouts reported a small Xia camp, and the Song pressed on.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，福與懌循好水川西去，未至羊牧隆城五里，與夏軍遇。

translations.literal: At dawn Fu and Yi followed the Haoshui westward; before reaching within five li of Yangmulong City they met the Xia army.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Fu and Yi marched west along the Haoshui. Five li short of Yangmulong City they met the Xia army.

sentences.zh: 懌爲先鋒，見道傍置數銀泥合，封襲謹密，中有動躍聲，疑莫敢發，福至發之，乃懸哨家鴿百餘，自合中起，盤飛軍上。

translations.literal: Yi as vanguard saw several silver paste boxes placed by the road, sealed tightly; inside were jumping sounds; he suspected and dared not open them; when Fu arrived and opened them, more than a hundred tethered carrier pigeons rose from the boxes and circled above the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, in the van, found several silver paste boxes beside the road, tightly sealed, with something moving inside. He dared not open them until Fu arrived. When they were opened, more than a hundred carrier pigeons rose and circled overhead—signaling the trap.

sentences.zh: 于是夏兵四合，懌先犯，中軍繼之，自辰至午酣戰。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xia troops closed in from four sides; Yi attacked first, the central army followed, and from the chen hour to the wu hour they fought fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Xia troops closed in from every side. Yi struck first, the main body followed, and from mid-morning to noon the battle raged.

sentences.zh: 陣中忽樹鮑老旗，長二丈餘，懌等莫測。

translations.literal: Suddenly in the battle line a "Bao Lao" banner was raised, more than two zhang long; Yi and the others could not fathom it.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a Bao Lao banner more than two zhang high rose in the Xia line, and Yi and his men could not tell what it meant.

sentences.zh: 既而鮑老揮右則右伏出，揮左則左伏出，翼而襲之，宋師大敗。

translations.literal: Then when Bao Lao waved right, right ambush emerged; when he waved left, left ambush emerged; flanking they struck, and the Song army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao Lao signaled right, ambushers sprang from the right; when he signaled left, from the left. They struck from both flanks and the Song army was shattered.

sentences.zh: 懌、劉肅及福子懷亮皆戰沒。

translations.literal: Yi, Liu Su, and Fu's son Huailiang all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, Liu Su, and Fu's son Huailiang all fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 小校劉進勸福自拔，福不聽，力戰死。

translations.literal: Junior officer Liu Jin urged Fu to break out himself; Fu would not listen and fought to death.
translations.idiomatic: A junior officer, Liu Jin, urged Fu to break out; Fu refused and fought until he was killed.

sentences.zh: 初，渭州都監趙津將瓦亭塞騎兵三千余爲諸將後繼。

translations.literal: At first Wei Prefecture garrison commander Zhao Jin commanded more than three thousand cavalry from Wating Stockade as rear support for the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wei Prefecture garrison commander Zhao Jin had marched more than three thousand cavalry from Wating Stockade as the army's reserve.

sentences.zh: 是日，朱觀、武英兵會能家川與夏人遇，陣合，王珪自羊牧隆城以屯兵四千五百人助觀略陣，陣堅不可動，英重傷，不能出軍戰。

translations.literal: That day Zhu Guan and Wu Ying's troops joined at Nengjia Stream and met Xia troops; battle lines formed; Wang Gui from Yangmulong City brought garrison troops of four thousand five hundred to help Guan array the line; the formation was firm and could not be moved; Ying was gravely wounded and could not lead troops to fight.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Guan and Ying joined at Nengjia Stream and clashed with the Xia. Wang Gui marched forty-five hundred garrison troops from Yangmulong to help Guan hold the line. The formation stood firm but could not advance; Wu Ying was gravely wounded and could not fight.

sentences.zh: 自午至申，夏軍益至，東陣步兵大潰，衆遂奔。

translations.literal: From wu to shen the Xia army increased; the eastern formation's foot soldiers broke in great rout and the host fled.
translations.idiomatic: From noon to mid-afternoon more Xia troops arrived. The eastern wing's infantry collapsed and the army fled.

sentences.zh: 珪、英、津及參軍耿傅、隊將李簡、都監李禹享、劉均皆死于陣。

translations.literal: Gui, Ying, Jin, staff officer Geng Fu, squad leader Li Jian, garrison commander Li Yuxiang, and Liu Jun all died on the field.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui, Wu Ying, Zhao Jin, staff officer Geng Fu, squad leader Li Jian, garrison commander Li Yuxiang, and Liu Jun all died on the field.

sentences.zh: 觀以千餘人保民垣，發矢四射，會暮，夏軍引去。

translations.literal: Guan with more than a thousand men defended a village wall, shooting arrows in four directions; at dusk the Xia army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Guan held a village wall with a thousand men, shooting in every direction until dusk, when the Xia withdrew.

sentences.zh: 將校士卒死者萬三百人，關右震動。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers who died numbered ten thousand three hundred, and the lands west of the Pass were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand three hundred officers and soldiers had been killed, and the lands west of the Pass were shaken.

sentences.zh: 軍須日廣，三司告不足，仁宗爲之旰食，宋庠請修潼關以備衝突。

translations.literal: Military supplies daily grew broader; the Three Departments reported insufficiency; Emperor Renzong on its account ate late; Song Qi requested to repair Tong Pass to guard against sudden attack.
translations.idiomatic: Military requirements grew daily. The Three Departments reported shortages, and Emperor Renzong lost his appetite over it. Song Qi requested that Tong Pass be fortified against sudden raids.

sentences.zh: 秋，夏人轉攻河東，及麟、府，不能下，乃引兵攻豐州，城孤無援，遂據之；

translations.literal: In autumn, the Xia people turned to attack Hedong and Lin and Fu, could not take them, then led troops to attack Feng Prefecture; the city was isolated without aid, and they thereupon seized it.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn the Xia turned to attack Hedong and the prefectures of Lin and Fu. Failing to take them, they marched on Feng Prefecture, which stood isolated without relief, and seized it.

sentences.zh: 又破寧遠砦，屯要害，絕麟、府餉道。

translations.literal: They again broke Ningyuan Fort, encamped at a strategic pass, and cut off the supply route of Lin and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: They next captured Ningyuan Fort, stationed troops at a key choke point, and severed the supply lines to Lin and Fu.

sentences.zh: 楊偕始請棄河外，保合河津，帝不許。

translations.literal: Yang Xie at first requested to abandon the lands beyond the river and hold the ford at Hehe; the Emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xie initially urged abandoning the territories beyond the river and holding only the Hehe crossing, but the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 會張亢管勾麟府軍馬事，破之于柏子，又破之于兔毛川，亢築十餘柵，河外始固。

translations.literal: At this time Zhang Kang was in charge of Lin and Fu military horse affairs; he defeated them at Baizi and again at Tumaoyan; Kang built more than ten stockades, and the lands beyond the river first became secure.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Zhang Kang, who oversaw military affairs at Lin and Fu, routed the Xia at Baizi and again at Rabbit-Fur Stream. He built more than ten fortified posts, and for the first time the lands beyond the river stood secure.

sentences.zh: 元昊雖數勝，然死亡創痍者相半，人困于點集，財力不給，國中爲「十不如」之謠以怨之。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao although repeatedly victorious, yet those dead and wounded amounted to half; the people were exhausted by conscription; wealth and strength could not supply; within the state a song of "ten not-as-good-as" was made to resent him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yuan Hao won battle after battle, casualties and wounded amounted to half his forces. The people were worn down by conscription, the treasury could not keep up, and within his realm a lampoon called the "Ten Not-As-Good-As" circulated to voice their resentment.

sentences.zh: 元昊乃歸塞門砦主高延德，因乞和，知延州范仲淹爲書陳禍福以喻之。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao then returned Gao Yande, commander of the Saimen Fort, and thereby begged peace; Fan Zhongyan, prefect of Yan Prefecture, wrote a letter setting forth blessings and calamities to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao returned Gao Yande, the commander of Saimen Fort, and sued for peace. Fan Zhongyan, prefect of Yanzhou, wrote to him explaining the consequences of war and peace.

sentences.zh: 元昊使其親信野利旺榮復書，語猶嫚。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao had his close follower Yeli Wangrong reply with a letter; the language was still insolent.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao had his confidant Yeli Wangrong reply, but the tone remained insulting.

sentences.zh: 知延州龐籍言，夏境鼠食稼，且旱，元昊思納款，遂令知保安軍劉拯諭旺榮言：「公方持靈、夏兵，倘內附，當以西平茅土分冊之。

translations.literal: Prefect of Yan Prefecture Pang Ji said: in Xia territory rats ate the grain, and moreover there was drought; Yuan Hao thought to submit in good faith; he then ordered Liu Zheng, commander of Bao'an Army, to instruct Wangrong, saying: "You presently hold the troops of Ling and Xia; if you come over to us, we shall enfeoff you as Lord of Xiping with a fief."
translations.idiomatic: Pang Ji, prefect of Yanzhou, reported that rats were devouring the crops in Xia territory and drought had set in. Yuan Hao was inclined to sue for peace, and had Liu Zheng of Bao'an Army tell Wangrong: "You command the armies of Ling and Xia. If you defect to us, we shall enfeoff you as Lord of Xiping with a domain of your own."

sentences.zh: 」知青澗城種世衡又遣王嵩以棗及畫龜爲書置蠟丸中遺旺榮，諭以早歸之意，欲元昊得之，疑旺榮。

translations.literal: Prefect of Qingjian City Zhong Shihang also sent Wang Song with jujubes and a painted turtle as a letter placed in a wax pellet and presented to Wangrong, instructing him on the intent of early submission, wishing Yuan Hao to obtain it and suspect Wangrong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Shihang of Qingjian City also sent Wang Song to Wangrong with a message sealed in a wax pellet—jujubes and a painted turtle—urging him to come over soon. The ploy was meant for Yuan Hao to intercept it and grow suspicious of Wangrong.

sentences.zh: 旺榮得之笑曰：「種使君亦長矣，何爲此兒戲耶！

translations.literal: Wangrong obtaining it laughed and said: "Commissioner Zhong is also aged; why perform this child's play!"
translations.idiomatic: When Wangrong received it he laughed and said, "Commissioner Zhong is no young man—why resort to such childish tricks?"

sentences.zh: 」囚嵩窖中歲餘。

translations.literal: He imprisoned Song in a cellar for more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: He kept Wang Song imprisoned in a cellar for more than a year.

sentences.zh: 知渭州王沿、總管葛懷敏使僧法淳持書往，而旺榮乃出嵩與教練使李文貴至青澗城，自言用兵以來，資用困乏，人情便于和。

translations.literal: Prefect of Wei Prefecture Wang Yan and commander-in-chief Ge Huaimin sent the monk Fachun bearing a letter, whereupon Wangrong then released Song and training commissioner Li Wen'gui to Qingjian City, saying of themselves that since employing troops, supplies were exhausted and strained, and popular sentiment favored peace.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan, prefect of Weizhou, and the commander Ge Huaimin sent the monk Fachun with a letter. Wangrong then released Wang Song along with the training commissioner Li Wen'gui to Qingjian City, explaining that since the war began supplies had run short and the people favored peace.

sentences.zh: 籍疑其款吾軍，留之數月。

translations.literal: Ji suspected their good faith toward our army and detained them several months.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Ji suspected they were negotiating in bad faith and kept them for several months.

sentences.zh: 二年，復大入，戰于定川，宋師大敗，葛懷敏死之。

translations.literal: In the second year, they again invaded on a large scale; battle was at Dingchuan; the Song army was greatly defeated; Ge Huaimin died in it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the war the Xia invaded again in force. At Dingchuan the Song army suffered a crushing defeat, and Ge Huaimin was killed.

sentences.zh: 直抵渭州，大焚掠而去。

translations.literal: They straightway reached Wei Prefecture, burned and plundered greatly, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They pushed all the way to Weizhou, burned and plundered on a vast scale, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔籍招納，籍遣文貴還。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ji to recruit and receive them; Ji sent Wen'gui back.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Pang Ji to negotiate their submission, and he sent Li Wen'gui back.

sentences.zh: 月余，元昊使文貴與王嵩以其臣旺榮、其弟旺令、嵬名環、臥譽諍三人書議和，然屈強不肯削僭號，且雲「如日方中，止可順天西行，安可逆天東下。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Yuan Hao had Wen'gui and Wang Song with letters from his ministers Wangrong, his younger brother Wangling, Weiming Huan, and Woyu Zheng discuss peace, yet stubbornly refusing to renounce his usurped title, and moreover saying: "Like the sun at its zenith, one can only follow Heaven and go west; how can one defy Heaven and go east?"
translations.idiomatic: After another month Yuan Hao sent Li Wen'gui and Wang Song with letters from his ministers Wangrong, his brother Wangling, Weiming Huan, and Woyu Zheng to discuss peace. Yet he remained defiant, refusing to abandon his imperial title, declaring: "The sun stands at its zenith—it can only follow Heaven westward. How could it defy Heaven and travel east?"

sentences.zh: 」籍以其言未服，乃令自請，而詔籍復書許之。

translations.literal: Ji, because their words were not submissive, then ordered them to petition themselves, while an edict ordered Ji to reply in writing granting it.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Ji found their language insufficiently deferential and required them to submit a formal petition. The court then instructed him to reply granting their request.

sentences.zh: 明年，遣六宅使伊州剌史賀從勖與文貴俱來，猶稱男邦泥定國兀卒上書父大宋皇帝，更名曩霄而不稱臣。

translations.literal: The next year, he sent the Commissioner of the Six Residences, Prefect of Yizhou He Congxu, together with Wen'gui, both coming; they still styled themselves "Male State of Niding, State-lord Wu Zu writing to father, the Great Song Emperor," changing the name to Nang Xiao and not calling themselves subject.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yuan Hao sent the Commissioner of the Six Residences and Prefect of Yizhou, He Congxu, together with Li Wen'gui. They still addressed the letter as "the Lord Wu Zu of the State of Niding to his father, the Emperor of Great Song," adopting the name Nang Xiao instead of acknowledging vassal status.

sentences.zh: 兀卒，即吾祖也，如可汗號。

translations.literal: Wu Zu means "our ancestor," like the title of khan.
translations.idiomatic: "Wu Zu" meant "Our Ancestor," equivalent to a khan's title.

sentences.zh: 議者以爲改吾祖爲兀卒，特以侮玩朝廷，不可許。

translations.literal: Deliberators considered that changing "our ancestor" to Wu Zu was specially to insult and mock the court; it could not be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Court commentators argued that substituting "Our Ancestor" with "Wu Zu" was a deliberate insult to the throne and could not be accepted.

sentences.zh: 詔遣邵良佐、張士元、張子奭、王正倫更往議，且許封冊爲夏國主，而元昊亦遣如定、聿舍、張延壽、楊守素繼來。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Shao Liangzuo, Zhang Shiyuan, Zhang Zishuang, and Wang Zhenglun to go again to negotiate, and moreover permitted investiture as Lord of the State of Xia; Yuan Hao also sent Ruding, Yushe, Zhang Yanshou, and Yang Shousu in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Shao Liangzuo, Zhang Shiyuan, Zhang Zishuang, and Wang Zhenglun back to negotiate and agreed to invest Yuan Hao as Lord of the State of Xia. Yuan Hao in turn dispatched Ruding, Yushe, Zhang Yanshou, and Yang Shousu.

sentences.zh: 四年，始上誓表言：「兩失和好，遂曆七年，立誓自今，願藏盟府。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he first submitted an oath memorial saying: "Both sides lost good relations, and it has already passed seven years; we establish an oath from now; we wish it stored in the covenant archive."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Yuan Hao at last submitted a sworn memorial: "Peace was broken on both sides and seven years have passed. We swear an oath from this day forward and ask that it be preserved in the covenant archive."

sentences.zh: 其前日所掠將校民戶，各不復還。

translations.literal: Those commanders, soldiers, and households plundered on former days shall each not be returned.
translations.idiomatic: Officers, soldiers, and civilians seized in earlier raids shall not be returned.

sentences.zh: 自此有邊人逃亡，亦毋得襲逐。

translations.literal: From this time if border people flee, neither side may also pursue in raid.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter neither side may pursue or seize border people who flee across the frontier.

sentences.zh: 臣近以本國城砦進納朝廷，其栲栳、鎌刀、南安、承平故地及他邊境蕃漢所居，乞畫中爲界，于內聽築城堡。

translations.literal: Your subject recently presented the forts and strongholds of this state to the court; the former lands of Kaolao, Liandao, Nan'an, and Chengping and where other border Fan and Han dwell—we beg to draw the middle as boundary; within it permit building fortresses and walls.
translations.idiomatic: I have recently surrendered the fortresses of my realm to the court. I ask that the former territories of Kaolao, Liandao, Nan'an, and Chengping, along with other borderlands where Tangut and Han peoples live, be divided down the middle as a boundary, with permission to build fortifications on my side.

sentences.zh: 凡歲賜銀、綺、絹、茶二十五萬五千，乞如常數，臣不復以他相干。

translations.literal: In all the yearly grants of silver, brocade, silk, and tea totaling two hundred fifty-five thousand, we beg as the usual numbers; your subject will no more interfere on other matters.
translations.idiomatic: As for the annual gifts of silver, brocade, silk, and tea totaling two hundred fifty-five thousand units, I ask that they continue at the customary rate, and I shall raise no other demands.

sentences.zh: 乞頒誓詔，蓋欲世世遵守，永以爲好。

translations.literal: We beg the issuance of the oath edict, meaning to observe it generation after generation and forever take it as friendship.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the sworn edict be promulgated so that it may be honored generation after generation and peace endure forever.

sentences.zh: 倘君親之義不存，或臣子之心渝變，使宗祀不永，子孫罹殃。

translations.literal: If the righteousness between lord and subject does not remain, or the heart of minister and son changes, causing the ancestral sacrifices not to endure, descendants will suffer calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Should the bond between sovereign and subject be broken, or loyalty give way to treachery, may our ancestral rites be cut short and our descendants suffer for it.

sentences.zh: 」詔答曰：「朕臨制四海，廓地萬里，西夏之土，世以爲胙。

translations.literal: The edict replied: "We rule the four seas, extending territory ten thousand li; the lands of Western Xia have from generation served as Our fief."
translations.idiomatic: The reply edict read: "We govern the four seas across a realm of ten thousand li. The lands of Western Xia have long served as Our fief."

sentences.zh: 今乃納忠悔咎，表于信誓，質之日月，要之鬼神，及諸子孫，無有渝變。

translations.literal: Now you have presented loyalty and repented faults, expressed in sworn faith, pledged to sun and moon, bound to spirits, and to all descendants—there shall be no change or alteration.
translations.idiomatic: Now you have submitted in loyalty and repented your errors, sealing your pledge before sun and moon, spirits, and posterity, without deviation.

sentences.zh: 申復懇至，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Stated repeatedly with earnest sincerity; We greatly commend it.
translations.idiomatic: Your sincerity, stated again and again, greatly pleases Us.

sentences.zh: 俯閱來誓，一皆如約。

translations.literal: Looking down to review the oath submitted, all accord with the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Having reviewed your sworn submission, We accept every provision.

sentences.zh: 」十二月，遣尚書祠部員外郎張子奭充冊禮使，東頭供奉官、閣門祗候張士元副之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, dispatched Minister of Rites Associate Zhang Zishuang as investiture envoy; Eastern Head Attendant-in-Waiting and Gate Keeper Zhang Shiyuan as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the court dispatched Zhang Zishuang, Associate in the Ministry of Rites, as investiture envoy, with Zhang Shiyuan, Attendant-in-Waiting and Gate Keeper, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 仍賜對衣、黃金帶、銀鞍勒馬、銀二萬兩、絹二萬匹、茶三萬斤。

translations.literal: Moreover granted matching robes, golden belt, silver saddle and bridle with horse, twenty thousand taels of silver, twenty thousand bolts of silk, thirty thousand jin of tea.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao was also granted a set of matching robes, a gold belt, a horse with silver saddle and bridle, twenty thousand taels of silver, twenty thousand bolts of silk, and thirty thousand jin of tea.

sentences.zh: 冊以漆書竹簡，籍以天下樂錦。

translations.literal: The investiture document was written in lacquer on bamboo slips; the register was on "All Under Heaven Rejoices" brocade.
translations.idiomatic: The patent of investiture was written in lacquer on bamboo slips, bound in brocade patterned with "All Under Heaven Rejoices."

sentences.zh: 金塗銀印，方二寸一分，文曰「夏國主印」，錦綬，塗金銀牌。

translations.literal: A gold-plated silver seal, square two cun one fen, inscription reading "Seal of the Lord of the State of Xia," brocade cord, gold-plated silver plaque.
translations.idiomatic: He received a silver seal plated with gold, two cun and one fen square, inscribed "Seal of the Lord of the State of Xia," with brocade cords and a gold-plated silver plaque.

sentences.zh: 緣冊法物，皆銀裝金塗，覆以紫繡。

translations.literal: The accompanying investiture ritual objects were all silver-mounted and gold-plated, covered with purple embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual implements accompanying the patent were all silver-mounted and gilt, wrapped in purple embroidery.

sentences.zh: 約稱臣，奉正朔，改所賜敕書爲詔而不名，許自置官屬。

translations.literal: By agreement he styled himself subject, observed the official calendar, changed the granted imperial rescript to edict without naming him, and was permitted to appoint his own officials.
translations.idiomatic: By agreement Yuan Hao acknowledged vassal status, adopted the Song calendar, and received edicts that addressed him without using his personal name. He was permitted to appoint his own officials.

sentences.zh: 使至京，就驛貿賣，宴坐朵殿。

translations.literal: When envoys reached the capital, they traded at the post station; banquets were held in the Duo Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia envoys reached the capital they were permitted to trade at their lodgings, and received banquets in the Duo Hall.

sentences.zh: 使至其國，相見用賓客禮。

translations.literal: When envoys reached their state, meetings used guest protocol.
translations.idiomatic: When Song envoys arrived in Xia territory they were received with guest ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 置榷場于保安軍及高平砦，第不通青鹽。

translations.literal: Established trade markets at Bao'an Army and Gaoping Fort; only green salt was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Trade markets were established at Bao'an Army and Gaoping Fort, though trade in green salt was prohibited.

sentences.zh: 然宋每遣使往，館于宥州，終不復至興、靈，而元昊帝其國中自若也。

translations.literal: Yet whenever Song dispatched envoys, they were lodged at You Prefecture and never again reached Xing and Ling; yet Yuan Hao acted as emperor within his state as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever the Song sent envoys they were housed at Youzhou and never permitted to reach Xingzhou or Lingzhou, while Yuan Hao continued to reign as emperor within his own realm undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，遼夾山部落呆兒族八百戶歸元昊，興宗責還，元昊不遣。

translations.literal: That year, eight hundred households of the Dair clan of the Jia Mountain tribe of Liao went over to Yuan Hao; Emperor Xingzong demanded their return; Yuan Hao did not send them back.
translations.idiomatic: That year eight hundred households of the Dair clan from Lia's Jia Mountain tribes defected to Yuan Hao. Emperor Xingzong of Liao demanded their return, but Yuan Hao refused to surrender them.

sentences.zh: 遂親將騎兵十萬出金肅城，弟天齊王馬步軍大元帥將騎七千出南路，韓國王將兵六萬出北路，三路濟河長驅。

translations.literal: Thereupon he personally led one hundred thousand cavalry out from Jinsu City; his younger brother the Prince of Tianqi, Grand Marshal of Horse and Foot, led seven thousand cavalry out on the southern route; the King of Han led sixty thousand troops out on the northern route; three routes crossed the river and drove deep.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong thereupon personally led one hundred thousand cavalry from Jinsu City. His brother the Prince of Tianqi, Grand Marshal of Horse and Foot, took seven thousand horsemen on the southern route, while the King of Han marched sixty thousand troops on the northern route. All three armies crossed the river and drove deep into Xia territory.

sentences.zh: 興宗入夏境四百里，不見敵，據得勝寺南壁以待。

translations.literal: Xingzong entered Xia territory four hundred li, saw no enemy, and occupied the southern rampart of Desheng Temple to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong penetrated four hundred li into Xia territory without encountering the enemy and encamped on the southern face of Desheng Temple to await battle.

sentences.zh: 八月五日，韓國王自賀蘭北與元昊接戰，數勝之。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the eighth month, the King of Han from north of Helan engaged Yuan Hao in battle and repeatedly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the eighth month the King of Han, advancing from north of Helan, clashed with Yuan Hao and won successive victories.

sentences.zh: 遼兵至者日益，夏乃請和，退十里，韓國王不從。

translations.literal: Liao troops arriving daily increased; Xia then begged peace and retreated ten li; the King of Han did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: As Liao reinforcements arrived daily, the Xia sued for peace and withdrew ten li, but the King of Han refused to accept.

sentences.zh: 如是退者三，凡百餘里矣，每退必赭其地，遼馬無所食，因許和。

translations.literal: Thus they retreated three times, altogether more than one hundred li; each time they retreated they must have scorched the earth; Liao horses had nothing to eat; therefore they permitted peace.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew three times in this manner, covering more than one hundred li in all. Each retreat was accompanied by scorched-earth tactics, leaving the Liao horses without forage, and at last peace was granted.

sentences.zh: 夏乃遷延，以老其師，而遼之馬益病，因急攻之，遂敗，復攻南壁，興宗大敗。

translations.literal: Xia then delayed, to wear out their army; and Liao horses grew sicker; therefore they urgently attacked and were defeated; again attacking the southern rampart, Xingzong was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia then dragged out negotiations to exhaust the invaders while the Liao horses sickened. Yuan Hao launched a sudden attack and routed them, then struck the southern encampment and dealt Xingzong a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 入南樞王蕭孝友砦，擒其鶻突姑駙馬，興宗從數騎走，元昊縱其去。

translations.literal: Entering the fort of Southern Pivot King Xiao Xiaoyou, they captured his Gudugu son-in-law; Xingzong fled with several riders; Yuan Hao let him go.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao stormed the camp of the Southern Pivot King Xiao Xiaoyou and captured his son-in-law Gudugu. Xingzong fled with a handful of riders, and Yuan Hao let him escape.

sentences.zh: 元昊五月五日生，國人以其日相慶賀，又以四孟朔爲節。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao was born on the fifth day of the fifth month; the people of the state on that day congratulated one another in celebration; they also took the four first days of seasons as festivals.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao was born on the fifth day of the fifth month, which the people celebrated as a national holiday. The first days of the four seasons were also observed as festivals.

sentences.zh: 凡五娶，一曰大遼興平公主，二曰宣穆惠文皇后沒藏氏，生諒祚，三曰憲成皇后野力氏，四曰妃沒𠼪氏，五曰索氏。

translations.literal: In all he took five wives: first, the Princess of Great Liao Xingping; second, Empress Xuanmu Huiven of the Mo Zang clan, who bore Liangzuo; third, Empress Xiancheng of the Yeli clan; fourth, consort of the Moyi clan; fifth, the Suo clan.
translations.idiomatic: He took five wives in all: first, the Liao Princess Xingping; second, Empress Xuanmu Huiven of the Mo clan, who bore Liangzuo; third, Empress Xiancheng of the Yeli clan; fourth, a consort of the Moyi clan; fifth, Lady Suo.

sentences.zh: 元昊以慶曆八年正月殂，年四十六。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao died in the first month of the eighth year of Qingli, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao died in the first month of Qingli 8 (1048), at the age of forty-six.

sentences.zh: 在位十七年，改元開運一年，廣運二年，大慶二年，天授禮法延祚十一年。

translations.literal: On the throne seventeen years; changed era names: Kaiyun one year, Guangyun two years, Daqing two years, Tianshou Lifafa Yanzuo eleven years.
translations.idiomatic: He reigned for seventeen years, using the era names Kaiyun (one year), Guangyun (two years), Daqing (two years), and Tianshou Lifafa Yanzuo (eleven years).

sentences.zh: 諡曰武烈皇帝，廟號景宗，墓號泰陵。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Emperor Wulie; temple name Emperor Jing; tomb name Tailing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Emperor Wulie, with the temple name Emperor Jing and the tomb name Tailing.

sentences.zh: 宋遣開封府判官、尚書祠部員外郎曹穎叔爲祭奠使，六宅使、達州刺史鄧保信爲吊慰使，賜絹一千匹、布五百端、羊百口、面米各百石、酒百瓶。

translations.literal: Song dispatched Kaifeng Prefecture judge and Minister of Rites Associate Cao Yingshu as sacrificial envoy; Commissioner of Six Residences and Prefect of Dazhou Deng Baoxin as condolence envoy; granted one thousand bolts of silk, five hundred bolts of cloth, one hundred sheep, flour and rice each one hundred shi, one hundred jars of wine.
translations.idiomatic: The Song dispatched Cao Yingshu, judge of Kaifeng Prefecture and Associate in the Ministry of Rites, as sacrificial envoy, and Deng Baoxin, Commissioner of the Six Residences and Prefect of Dazhou, as condolence envoy, with gifts of one thousand bolts of silk, five hundred bolts of cloth, one hundred sheep, one hundred shi each of flour and rice, and one hundred jars of wine.

sentences.zh: 及葬，仍賜絹一千五百匹，余如初賻。

translations.literal: At the burial, still granted one thousand five hundred bolts of silk; the rest as at the first condolence gifts.
translations.idiomatic: At the burial the Song granted an additional fifteen hundred bolts of silk, with the other gifts unchanged from the initial offering.

sentences.zh: 子諒祚立。

translations.literal: His son Liangzuo was established.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liangzuo succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐元年，母沒藏氏薨，遣祖儒嵬多、聿則慶唐及徐舜卿來告哀，詔以集賢校理馮浩假尚書刑部郎中、直史館爲吊慰使，文思副使張惟清假文思使副之，乃獻遺留馬駝以謝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiayou, his mother the Mo Zang clan died; dispatched Zuru Weiduo, Yuzhe Qingtang, and Xu Shunqing to announce mourning; an edict appointed Academician Editor Feng Hao, acting as Minister of Justice Associate and Direct Historiographer, as condolence envoy; Assistant Wensi Commissioner Zhang Weiqing acting as Wensi Commissioner as deputy; they then presented leftover horses and camels in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou 1 (1056) Liangzuo's mother, of the Mo clan, died. He sent Zuru Weiduo, Yuzhe Qingtang, and Xu Shunqing to announce her death. The court appointed Feng Hao, Academician Editor and acting Associate Minister of Justice, as condolence envoy, with Zhang Weiqing, Assistant Wensi Commissioner, as deputy. The Xia envoys presented horses and camels in gratitude for the gifts left at court.

sentences.zh: 諒祚幼養于母族訛龐，訛龐因專國政。

translations.literal: Liangzuo in youth was raised by his mother's clan Ebo; Ebo thereby monopolized state power.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzuo had been raised from childhood by his mother's clan, the Ebo, who consequently seized control of the government.

sentences.zh: 初，麟州西城枕睥睨曰紅樓，下瞰屈野河，其外距夏境尚七十里，而田腴利厚，多入訛龐，歲東侵不已。

translations.literal: At first, the western city of Lin Prefecture leaned on a watchtower called Red Tower, overlooking Quye River; beyond it the distance to Xia territory was still seventy li, yet the fields were fertile and profits rich; much fell into Ebo's hands; year by year they invaded eastward without cease.
translations.idiomatic: West of Lin Prefecture stood a watchtower called Red Tower overlooking the Quye River. Though still seventy li from Xia territory, the land there was fertile and profitable, and much of it had fallen under Ebo's control. Each year he raided eastward without letup.

sentences.zh: 至耕獲時，輒屯兵河西，經略使龐籍每戒邊將使毋得過屈野河，然所距屈野河猶二十里。

translations.literal: At planting and harvest seasons, they always encamped troops west of the river; frontier commissioner Pang Ji repeatedly warned border generals not to cross Quye River, yet the distance they were kept from Quye River was still twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: At planting and harvest time Ebo stationed troops west of the river. Frontier commissioner Pang Ji repeatedly ordered border commanders not to cross the Quye River, though they were still permitted to operate as far as twenty li from its banks.

sentences.zh: 管勾軍馬司賈逵徼循，見所侵田，稍過督邊吏，麟州守王亮懼，始以事聞。

translations.literal: Supervisor of military horse affairs Jia Kui on patrol saw the encroached fields, slightly exceeded bounds in pressing border officials; Lin Prefecture defender Wang Liang feared, and first reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui of the Military Horse Office, on patrol, discovered the encroached fields and pressed border officials slightly beyond their mandate. Lin Prefecture's commander Wang Liang, alarmed, reported the matter to the court for the first time.

sentences.zh: 詔以殿直張安世、賈恩爲同巡檢經制之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Palace Attendant Zhang Anshi and Jia En as joint patrol commissioners to manage it.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Palace Attendants Zhang Anshi and Jia En as joint patrol commissioners to handle the dispute.

sentences.zh: 訛龐晏然弗革，迫之則格鬥，緩之則歸耕，經略司遣使還所侵田，訛龐專爲濫言，無歸意。

translations.literal: Ebo was calm and did not reform; when pressed he fought; when relaxed he returned to farming; the frontier commission sent envoys to recover the encroached fields; Ebo specialized in wild talk and had no intent to return.
translations.idiomatic: Ebo remained unmoved. Press him and he fought; relax pressure and he went back to farming. The frontier commission sent envoys to demand return of the seized land, but Ebo responded with evasive pretexts and showed no intention of yielding.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐二年，遂團兵宿境上。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiayou, he then gathered troops and encamped on the border.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou 2 (1057) he massed troops and encamped on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 逮三月，增至數萬人，守將斂兵弗與戰。

translations.literal: Reaching three months, they increased to tens of thousands; the defending generals gathered in troops and did not engage in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Within three months his force swelled to tens of thousands. The Song defenders held their troops in check and declined battle.

sentences.zh: 知麟州武戡築堡于河西，以爲保障。

translations.literal: Prefect of Lin Prefecture Wu Kan built a fort west of the river as a safeguard.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kan, prefect of Linzhou, began building a fort west of the river as a defensive strongpoint.

sentences.zh: 役既興，戡率將吏往按視，遇夏人于沙鼠浪，戡與管勾郭恩等欲止，而走馬承受黃道元以言脅之，遂夜進至臥牛峰，見烽舉，且鼓聲，道元猶不信，比明，至忽里堆，與夏人相去才數十步，遂合戰。

translations.literal: Once the labor was underway, Kan led officers to inspect; encountering Xia people at Shashulang, Kan and Supervisor Guo En and others wished to halt, but the mounted courier receiver Huang Daoyuan threatened them with words; they then advanced by night to Woniu Peak, saw beacon fires and also drum sounds, yet Daoyuan still did not believe; by dawn they reached Hulidui, only several tens of steps from the Xia people, and then joined battle.
translations.idiomatic: Once construction began, Wu Kan led his officers to inspect the site. At Shashulang they encountered Xia troops. Wu Kan and Guo En wanted to halt, but the mounted courier Huang Daoyuan threatened them into pressing on. They marched through the night to Woniu Peak, where beacons flared and drums sounded, yet Daoyuan still refused to believe an enemy was near. At dawn they reached Hulidui, barely thirty paces from the Xia force, and battle was joined.

sentences.zh: 自旦至食時，夏人四面合擊，衆大潰，戡走，恩與道元及兵馬監押劉慶等被執。

translations.literal: From dawn until mealtime, Xia people attacked from four sides in concert; the multitude greatly routed; Kan fled; En and Daoyuan and military supervisor Liu Qing and others were captured.
translations.idiomatic: From dawn until midmorning the Xia attacked from all sides. The Song force collapsed in rout. Wu Kan escaped, but Guo En, Huang Daoyuan, and the military supervisor Liu Qing were taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 安撫司遣李思道、孫兆往議疆事，而訛龐驁不聽。

translations.literal: The Pacification Commission sent Li Sidao and Sun Zhao to discuss border affairs, but Ebo arrogantly would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacification Commission sent Li Sidao and Sun Zhao to negotiate the border dispute, but Ebo arrogantly refused to hear them.

sentences.zh: 久之，太原府、代州兵馬鈐轄蘇安靜得夏國呂寧、拽浪撩黎來合議，乃築堠九，更新邊禁，要以違約則罷和市，自此始定。

translations.literal: After a long time, military commander of Taiyuan Prefecture and Daizhou Su Anjing obtained the Xia state's Lu Ning and Zhailang Liaoli to come jointly negotiate; then nine signal towers were built, border prohibitions renewed, the essential point being that breach of agreement would end the market trade; from this it first became settled.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Su Anjing, military commander of Taiyuan and Daizhou, brought the Xia negotiators Lu Ning and Zhailang Liaoli to the table. Nine signal towers were erected, border regulations updated, and trade was made contingent on observance of the agreement. The dispute was settled at last.

sentences.zh: 諒祚忌訛龐專，或告訛龐將叛，諒祚討殺之，夷其族。

translations.literal: Liangzuo resented Ebo's monopoly; someone reported Ebo would rebel; Liangzuo attacked and killed him, exterminating his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzuo resented Ebo's grip on power. When word reached him that Ebo planned rebellion, he struck first, killing Ebo and exterminating his clan.

sentences.zh: 已而請去蕃禮，從漢儀。

translations.literal: Shortly after, he requested to abandon Tangut rites and follow Han ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: He soon afterward asked to abandon Tangut customs and adopt Chinese court ceremony.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐六年，上書自言慕中國衣冠，明年當以此迎使者。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiayou, he submitted a memorial saying of himself that he admired Chinese dress and cap; the next year he would use this to receive envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou 6 (1061) he wrote to the court expressing admiration for Chinese dress and ceremony, pledging to receive Song envoys in Chinese style the following year.

sentences.zh: 詔許之。

translations.literal: An edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted permission.

sentences.zh: 明年，又改西壽監軍司爲保泰軍，石州監軍司爲靜塞軍，韋州監軍司爲祥祐軍，左廂監軍司爲神勇軍。

translations.literal: The next year, again changed Western Shou Military Commission to Baotai Army, Shizhou Military Commission to Jingsai Army, Weizhou Military Commission to Xiangyou Army, Left Wing Military Commission to Shenyong Army.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he renamed the Western Shou Military Commission as Baotai Army, the Shizhou commission as Jingsai Army, the Weizhou commission as Xiangyou Army, and the Left Wing commission as Shenyong Army.

sentences.zh: 遣人獻方物，稱宣徽南院使，詔諭非陪臣所宜稱，戒其僭擬，使遵誓詔。

translations.literal: He sent persons presenting local products, styling himself Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat; an edict instructed that this was not what an attendant minister should style; warned against presumptuous imitation; ordered compliance with the oath edict.
translations.idiomatic: He sent tribute while styling himself Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat. The court rebuked him, noting that such a title was improper for a vassal, warned him against presumption, and reminded him to honor the sworn treaty.

sentences.zh: 表求太宗御制詩章隸書石本，且進馬五十匹，求《九經》、《唐史》、《冊府元龜》及宋正至朝賀儀，詔賜《九經》，還所獻馬。

translations.literal: Memorial requested rubbed copies in clerical script on stone of poems composed by Emperor Taizong; moreover presented fifty horses; requested the Nine Classics, Tang History, Cefu Yuangui, and Song calendar and court ceremony; edict granted the Nine Classics and returned the horses presented.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he requested stone rubbings of Emperor Taizong's poems in clerical script, presented fifty horses, and asked for the Nine Classics, the Tang History, the Cefu Yuangui, and Song calendar and court ritual manuals. The court granted only the Nine Classics and returned his horses.

sentences.zh: 三年，遂大舉攻大順城，分兵圍柔遠砦，燒屈乞村，柵段木嶺，州兵、熟戶、蕃官趙明合擊退之。

translations.literal: In the third year, then on a large scale attacked Dashun City, divided troops to besiege Rouyuan Fort, burned Quqi Village, palisaded Duanmu Ridge; prefectural troops, settled tribes, and Fan official Zhao Ming jointly attacked and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he launched a major assault on Dashun City, detached troops to besiege Rouyuan Fort, burned Quqi Village, and fortified Duanmu Ridge. Prefectural troops, allied tribes, and the Tangut official Zhao Ming combined forces and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 遣西京左藏庫副使何次公詰之。

translations.literal: Dispatched Western Capital Left Treasury Deputy Commissioner He Cigong to interrogate them.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent He Cigong, Deputy Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Treasury, to demand an explanation.

sentences.zh: 三月，乃獻方物謝罪，賜絹五百匹、銀五百兩。

translations.literal: In the third month, then presented local products to apologize; granted five hundred bolts of silk and five hundred taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Liangzuo sent tribute to apologize. The court responded with five hundred bolts of silk and five hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，乃遣內殿崇班魏璪賜以治平三年冬服、銀絹。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong ascended, then dispatched Inner Hall Attendant Wei Sao to grant Zhizhi third-year winter garments, silver and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Upon Emperor Shenzong's accession the court sent Wei Sao, Inner Hall Attendant, with winter garments of Zhiping 3 (1066) and gifts of silver and silk.

sentences.zh: 供備庫副使高遵裕告哀，並以英宗遣留物賜之。

translations.literal: Provision Supply Deputy Commissioner Gao Zunyu announced mourning, and also granted the items Yingzong had left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zunyu, Deputy Commissioner of the Provision Supply Office, announced condolences on Yingzong's death and granted items the late emperor had bequeathed.

sentences.zh: 秋，夏國遣使奉慰及進助山陵。

translations.literal: In autumn, the State of Xia dispatched envoys to offer condolences and present aid for the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Western Xia sent envoys to offer condolences and contribute to the imperial burial.

sentences.zh: 冬，種諤取綏州，因發兵夜掩嵬名山帳，脅降之。

translations.literal: In winter, Zhong E captured Suizhou; then sent troops by night to surprise the camp of Weiming Shan, coercing his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zhong E seized Suizhou and launched a night raid on the camp of Weiming Shan, forcing his surrender.

sentences.zh: 諒祚乃詐爲會議，誘知保安軍楊定、都巡檢侍其臻等殺之，邊吏以聞，命韓琦知永興軍，經略西方。

translations.literal: Liangzuo then feigned a conference, lured Prefect of Bao'an Army Yang Ding, Chief Inspector Shiqizhen and others, and killed them; border officials reported it; Han Qi was appointed to Yongxing Army, to oversee the west.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzuo then lured Yang Ding, commander of Bao'an Army, and Chief Inspector Shiqizhen under the pretense of a conference and had them killed. When border officials reported the incident, Han Qi was appointed to Yongxing Army to oversee western defense.

sentences.zh: 諒祚錮送殺定者六宅使李崇貴、右侍禁韓道善及虜去定子仲通。

translations.literal: Liangzuo imprisoned and sent the killers: Commissioner of Six Residences Li Chonggui and Right Palace Guard Han Daoshan; and carried off Ding's son Zhongtong.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzuo imprisoned and surrendered the assassins—Li Chonggui, Commissioner of the Six Residences, and Han Daoshan, Right Palace Guard—and carried off Yang Ding's son Zhongtong.

sentences.zh: 十二月，諒祚殂，年二十一。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Liangzuo died, aged twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Liangzuo died at the age of twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 在位二十年，改元延嗣甯國一年，天祐垂聖三年，福聖承道四年，奲都六年，拱化五年。

translations.literal: On the throne twenty years; changed era names: Yansiningguo one year, Tianyou Chuishing three years, Fusheng Chengdiao four years, A'du six years, Gonghua five years.
translations.idiomatic: He reigned twenty years under the era names Yansiningguo (one year), Tianyou Chuishing (three years), Fusheng Chengdiao (four years), A'du (six years), and Gonghua (five years).

sentences.zh: 謚曰昭英皇帝，廟號毅宗，墓號安陵。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Emperor Zhaoying; temple name Emperor Yizong; tomb name Anling.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Emperor Zhaoying, with the temple name Emperor Yizong and the tomb name Anling.

sentences.zh: 子秉常立。

translations.literal: His son Bingchang was established.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bingchang succeeded to the throne.
